research_focus: Providing a user-friendly natural language interface for a complex blockchain-based farm-to-fork traceability platform by building a RAG-based LLM conversational agent that reduces the steep learning curve of blockchain technology for end users.
method: A RAG approach is used where a knowledge base (from PDFs and other documents) is processed with an embedding model and stored in a vector database. User queries are combined with a proximity search in the vector database, and the retrieved context is fed into an LLM that considers conversation history. Asynchronous delivery is handled via Server-Sent Events, and multimodal media (images, videos) are aggregated with the embeddings.
application_domain: Farm-to-fork food traceability and agricultural supply chain management on a blockchain platform
results_summary: The authors present a proof-of-concept RAG-based LLM chatbot that enables natural language interaction with a blockchain-based farm-to-fork traceability platform. The system retrieves relevant information via proximity search in a vector database and generates context-aware responses using an LLM, supporting multimodal content and asynchronous delivery. The chatbot is described as being primarily limited by its documentation and highly malleable in defining its knowledge domain without retraining the language model. The authors conclude that the RAG approach is feasible for this niche use case but note that the full traceability solution is still in the research phase and requires further validation with actual end users.
limitations: The chatbot is mostly limited by its documentation; The full traceability solution is still in the research phase; The system has not yet been tested with actual end users of the platform; Navigating the wide range of technological and architectural options in the ML space was a significant difficulty
research_gaps: Further testing with actual end users of the platform is required; Testing should incorporate upcoming releases of new LLM models; New approaches to context-aware conversational agents should be explored; The proof-of-concept needs to be adapted to the real-world business case

research_focus: Building a high-performance content-based image retrieval (CBIR) system that combines transfer learning with a vector database to improve both retrieval speed and accuracy on large-scale image datasets.
method: A pre-trained VGG-16 model is used via transfer learning to extract high-dimensional feature vectors from images. These vectors are stored and retrieved using the Milvus vector database. The system is evaluated on ImageClef, ImageNet, and Corel-1k datasets, comparing indexing and retrieval time and accuracy against a reference big-data solution.
application_domain: Content-based image retrieval (CBIR) on large-scale image datasets (ImageClef, ImageNet, Corel-1k); practical applications mentioned include e-commerce, web search, and medical image analysis.
results_summary: The proposed VCBIR system combines VGG-16 feature extraction with Milvus vector database indexing to achieve real-time image retrieval. Experiments on ImageClef, ImageNet, and Corel-1k show that the retrieval stage significantly outperforms the reference big-data solution, reducing retrieval time to approximately 1 second (several orders of magnitude improvement) while maintaining high precision and recall. The indexing stage, however, did not outperform the big-data solution, though the authors note indexing is typically performed offline. Overall, the system demonstrates that combining transfer learning with a vector database is effective for large-scale, real-time image retrieval.
limitations: Experiments were conducted using CPU only, not GPU, which limits performance and response speed; The system is limited to a single-machine environment and does not support distributed deployment; The indexing stage performance did not outperform the reference big-data solution
research_gaps: Migrate the system to GPU to significantly improve performance and response speed for large-scale image data; Transform the single-machine implementation into a distributed architecture to improve scalability, stability, reliability, and handling of high concurrent access

research_focus: Developing an LLM-powered chatbot (DrugRepoChatter) that uses a vector database of expert-curated open-access articles to provide efficient, accurate, and contextually relevant access to drug repurposing literature, addressing the challenge of navigating the overwhelming volume of scientific publications in this fast-evolving field.
method: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture: 285 expert-curated open-access articles are preprocessed, split into text chunks, and embedded into a vector space using an LLM model. User queries are embedded and matched via semantic similarity search against the stored embeddings; the most relevant text splits are retrieved and used by the LLM to generate grounded, source-cited answers.
application_domain: Drug repurposing / pharmaceutical research literature retrieval
results_summary: The authors developed DrugRepoChatter, a RAG-based chatbot built on a vector database of 285 expert-curated open-access drug repurposing articles, to streamline literature access for researchers. The system embeds article text splits into a vector space and retrieves relevant passages via semantic similarity matching, then generates answers grounded in the retrieved content with direct source citations. Initial user feedback indicated strong appreciation for the chatbot's intuitive design and the credibility of its responses. The tool successfully eliminates the need for researchers to manually navigate multiple databases and accelerates the identification of novel drug repurposing opportunities. The development demonstrates that combining expert curation with vector-based retrieval and LLM generation can significantly enhance the efficiency of scientific literature review in a specialized biomedical domain.
limitations: The knowledge base is limited to 285 statically curated articles and does not automatically incorporate new publications; Embedding and chatting with full-text articles would introduce computational demands and potential user experience issues, so new articles are limited to titles and abstracts; The effectiveness of the RAG approach depends on the quality and relevance of the curated literature collection used as the knowledge base

research_focus: Enhancing long-term context retention and task execution efficiency of LLM-based intelligences by proposing a vector-database-based long-term memory mechanism (VIMBank) that stores, retrieves, and dynamically updates historical interaction data to overcome context window limitations in multi-round complex tasks.
method: VIMBank stores sliced and vectorized historical interaction data (knowledge, dialog, task information) in a vector database, designs different retrieval strategies for different information types, and applies a dynamic memory updating strategy based on the Ebbinghaus forgetting curve theory to selectively forget unimportant memories and reinforce frequently accessed ones. The mechanism is evaluated on ALFWorld, HotpotQA, and KAgentBench multi-task datasets using open-source models (Qwen2-7b, chatglm3-6b) and closed-source models (ChatGPT), with agent frameworks ReACT and InterACT for task decomposition and reflection.
mentioned_systems: VIMBank; ReACT; InterACT; ChatGPT; Qwen2-7b; chatglm3-6b
application_domain: LLM agent multi-task planning and decision-making, continuous dialogue, personalized recommendations, healthcare, and education
results_summary: The paper proposes VIMBank, a vector storage-based long-term memory mechanism that addresses the context window limitation and high reasoning cost of LLMs in complex multi-round tasks. By storing vectorized historical interactions in a vector database and applying an Ebbinghaus forgetting curve–based dynamic update strategy, VIMBank enables selective memory retention and efficient retrieval. Experiments on ALFWorld, HotpotQA, and KAgentBench datasets demonstrate that VIMBank increases the task decision success rate by 10% to 20% and reduces reasoning cost by approximately 23% compared to baselines without long-term memory. The mechanism is shown to be versatile, adapting to both open-source models (Qwen2-7b, chatglm3-6b) and closed-source models (ChatGPT).
limitations: Existing long-term memory approaches for LLMs suffer from high storage and retrieval overhead and correctness problems; Memory mechanisms must support dynamic updates to avoid LLMs referencing outdated or irrelevant task-related information, which affects decision accuracy
research_gaps: Long-term memory support is still needed to enhance LLMs when persistent interaction is required and accuracy and efficiency must be guaranteed in multi-task scenarios; Future development of intelligences with long-term memory and adaptive learning ability requires further theoretical and practical support

research_focus: Mitigating jailbreak attacks (specifically Self Reminder attacks) on large language models by using a prompt-based filtering system (Prompt-G) that leverages vector databases and embedding techniques to detect and block malicious prompts in real time.
method: Prompt-G uses vector databases with embedding techniques (BERT-based embeddings) to store and retrieve representations of known jailbreak prompts, enabling similarity-based detection of harmful inputs. A dataset of Self Reminder attacks was collected and analyzed; K-means clustering (k=2) was applied to distinguish successful from failed jailbreak prompts. The system was integrated with the quantized Llama 2 13B chat model, and when a harmful prompt was detected, the model temperature was set to 0 to force a safe refusal response. Evaluation compared Prompt-G against baselines including Vanilla SFT, Aligned SFT, Goal Prioritization, and Self Reminder.
mentioned_systems: Prompt-G; Llama 2 13B; Llama (Meta); BERT; GPT; PaLM; Bloom
indexing_methods: LSH (locality-sensitive hashing); tree-based indexing; K-means clustering; BERT embeddings
application_domain: LLM security and adversarial robustness in natural language processing, specifically defense against prompt injection and jailbreak attacks on chat-based language models
results_summary: Prompt-G was evaluated against four attack types (fake news, phishing email, malicious information, SQL injection) and compared to four baseline methods. When integrated with Llama 2 13B, the attack success rate was reduced to 2.08%, outperforming all baselines. K-means clustering revealed that 77.33% of 75 system prompts were successful jailbreaks for fake news, with similar high success rates for phishing (81.08%), malicious content (82.43%), and SQL injection (74.32%). The system correctly identified 98.95% of harmful questions and 47 of 50 harmless questions, though a 6% false-positive rate was observed where harmless questions were misclassified as harmful due to semantic confusion.
limitations: 6% false-positive rate where harmless questions were misclassified as harmful due to semantic confusion; Minor tendency to incorrectly flag benign prompts as harmful, creating a trade-off between robust protection and response accuracy; Evaluation is focused on a specific model (Llama 2 13B) rather than a broad range of LLM architectures; Primarily designed and tested against Self Reminder attacks, with limited coverage of other jailbreak techniques
research_gaps: Evaluate the generalizability of the framework against other jailbreak techniques such as Role Play and Prompt Injection attacks; Investigate framework performance across diverse LLM architectures (e.g., GPT, PaLM, Bloom) with varying parameterization and training data; Enhance the model filter by increasing the heterogeneity and diversity of known jailbreak attacks and harmful questions in the database to reduce false positives and improve detection accuracy; Continuous adaptation and regular updates of LLMs to keep pace with the growing sophistication of jailbreak attacks

research_focus: Enhancing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems by integrating fine-tuned LLMs (via LoRA/QLoRA) with vector databases, and introducing a Quantized Influence Measure (QIM) as an 'AI Judge' mechanism to improve result selection precision in chatbot applications.

research_focus: Replacing subjective human visual comparison in nodular iron casting metallography classification with an objective, fast, computer-based similarity search method using a vector database, while avoiding the high computational cost and complexity of deep learning approaches.
method: A vector database is constructed from a characterized baseline metallography dataset. Each image is embedded using Local Binary Pattern (LBP) followed by Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for dimensionality reduction. At query time, Cosine Similarity is used to retrieve the k most similar stored metallographies, and a similarity-weighted average of their characterized values produces the final classification.
indexing_methods: LBP (Local Binary Pattern); PCA (Principal Component Analysis); Cosine Similarity; k-Nearest Neighbors
application_domain: Metallography analysis and quality control in iron foundries (nodular iron casting)
results_summary: The paper addresses the need for fast, objective metallography classification in foundries by proposing a similarity-search-based approach using a vector database. LBP embeddings with PCA dimensionality reduction were used to represent metallographies, and Cosine Similarity with k-NN retrieval was applied for classification. Optimal k values were determined to be k=2 for nodule count and k=21 for nodularity percentage, yielding a deviation of approximately 8 percentage units in the best cases. The system is described as pessimistic, meaning it avoids generating false positives. The authors conclude the method is feasible for day-to-day foundry use while being significantly simpler and faster than deep learning alternatives.
limitations: The dataset does not cover the full spectrum of possible metallography values, so unusual or laboratory/test images will not be well characterized; The deviation in optimal cases is around 8 percentage units, which may be insufficient for some applications; The method has only been tested on one type of iron (nodular iron) and one type of metallography (non-attacked); Vector representation relies on classical computer vision methods (LBP), which may be less accurate than newer deep learning-based embeddings; The system cannot handle images for which no sufficiently similar reference exists in the database

research_focus: How embedding dimensions and the density/descriptiveness of knowledge stored in a vector database influence the quality of text classification by text embedding models in the medical domain.
method: LLMs (gpt-3.5-turbo, flan-t5-xl, LLaMA-70b-chat) were used to generate query and ground-truth datasets for eight ailments. Ground truths were stored in a Pinecone vector database, queries were embedded using text embedding models (text-embedding-ada-002, text-embedding-gecko@001), and the most similar vector was selected as the classification. A robustness test framework (3 LLMs × 3 roles × 2 embedding models = 18 combinations) was used to evaluate accuracy and F1 score across different model pairings.
mentioned_systems: Pinecone; text-embedding-ada-002; text-embedding-gecko@001; gpt-3.5-turbo; flan-t5-xl; LLaMA-70b-chat; Med-PaLM
application_domain: Medical text classification: classifying patient symptoms and lab results into specific ailments (glaucoma, jaundice, cyanosis, psoriasis, conjunctivitis, scoliosis, skin cancer, gingivitis) using vector similarity search.
results_summary: The study validated that higher embedding dimensions (1536 vs. 768) and more descriptive data in the vector database lead to better medical text classification. The text-embedding-ada-002 model with 1536 dimensions consistently outperformed text-embedding-gecko@001 with 768 dimensions, particularly in distinguishing between similar ailments like skin cancer and psoriasis. Descriptive ground-truth data in the vector database was found to be more effective than sparse data, while short, concise queries (e.g., from flan-t5-xl) were still well-classified against a comprehensive knowledge base. The pipeline achieved low misclassification rates (as low as 3.63%) when a descriptive model generated the knowledge base and a general model generated queries, demonstrating that existing text embedding models and vector databases can serve as effective medical text classifiers without training multi-billion parameter LLMs.
limitations: Only eight ailments were tested, limiting the scope of the evaluation; Ground-truth data was generated by LLMs rather than curated by medical professionals, potentially introducing inconsistencies with accepted medical knowledge; The google-flan-t5-xl model generated sparse, keyword-level data that may not represent real-world medical knowledge bases; The study was conducted on a small scale and may not generalize to the full breadth of medical ailments with overlapping symptoms
research_gaps: Whether the classification success observed on eight ailments transfers to a much larger set of ailments with significant symptom overlap; Need for evaluation using datasets curated by medical professionals for more realistic test cases; Further work needed to determine whether the pipeline's effectiveness holds at scale across the full range of medical conditions

research_focus: Storage infrastructure best practices for enterprise LLM deployments, addressing performance, cost, and scalability challenges faced by businesses deploying large language models.
method: Analysis of recommended storage methods and structural elements based on industry studies and a real-world implementation case, with a focus on implications for decision makers and technical experts.
application_domain: Enterprise LLM deployment and business AI infrastructure
results_summary: The paper addresses storage infrastructure challenges in enterprise LLM deployments by examining recommended methods and structural elements for storage solutions. A real-world case study of a financial institution implementing a distributed NVMe storage system with a caching strategy achieved a 40% reduction in inference delay and a 35% decrease in storage costs while maintaining 99.999% uptime. The paper concludes that combining storage systems with caching techniques and monitoring mechanisms forms the foundation for enterprise-level LLM deployment.
research_gaps: Advancements in storage technology and growth potential for further enhancing efficiency over time; Preparing for future scalability requirements in enterprise LLM storage

Experimental trials and security analyses confirm the proposed approach is both robust and efficient for secure medical image retrieval.

research_focus: The paper addresses the problem of reliable and efficient person-job matching by proposing an end-to-end ANN-based technology (ResJobFit) that uses semantic similarity search with text embeddings to rank candidate suitability for job vacancies, achieving linear time complexity over quadratic pair-classification approaches.

research_focus: Reducing hallucination and improving interpretability of LLM responses in vertical/domain-specific settings by proposing a hybrid retrieval-augmented generation scheme (BM-RAGAM) that combines BM25 keyword matching with semantic association via attention mechanisms.
method: The authors developed BM-RAGAM, a hybrid joint retrieval strategy that assigns weights to mid-term results from BM25 keyword search and semantic-enhanced association using an attention mechanism. A vectorized knowledge base of ocean front and eddy text was constructed, and the scheme was integrated with the Qwen2-72B base LLM via the LangChain framework and OpenAI API. An ablation experiment and comparison against the fundamental Qwen2-72B model were conducted.
application_domain: Oceanography (ocean fronts and eddies) as a vertical domain for LLM-based intelligent Q&A
results_summary: The BM-RAGAM scheme was implemented by combining BM25 keyword retrieval with a semantic-enhanced attention-based association over a vectorized oceanographic knowledge base, integrated with the Qwen2-72B LLM. Compared to the fundamental Qwen2-72B baseline, the proposed scheme greatly reduced hallucination generation and produced more interpretable, factually grounded outputs. The hybrid retrieval with weighted attention ensured prioritization of the most pertinent information, improving response accuracy and relevance in the domain-specific setting. However, the outputs were observed to be less segmented than the baseline, potentially hindering comprehension for users who prefer structured responses. An ablation experiment confirmed the contribution of each retrieval component to the overall improvement.
limitations: BM-RAGAM outputs are less segmented than the baseline, which may impede text comprehension for general users who prefer structured and well-segmented responses; The attention mechanism's emphasis on relevance can reduce the granularity of information segmentation; Ethical considerations regarding data provenance and transparency for responsible use of retrieval-augmented systems need to be addressed

research_focus: Augmenting an aviation incident report dataset (ASRS) with ChatGPT via Retrieval Augmented Generation and a vector database to improve searching capability and provide accurate answers to safety-related queries for system safety assessment.
method: A Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline was constructed: word embeddings of ASRS incident reports were created using OpenAI's API and stored in a Pinecone vector database. When a user query is submitted, the most relevant reports are retrieved from the vector database and provided as context to ChatGPT, which then generates a summarised, sourced response.
application_domain: Aviation system safety and safety assessment (hazard identification, incident knowledge retrieval)
results_summary: The paper demonstrated that combining a Pinecone vector database with ChatGPT via RAG significantly improved answer accuracy for safety queries compared to standalone ChatGPT, which hallucinated incorrect information (e.g., claiming a Boeing 737 had never had a fuel leak). With RAG, two relevant incident reports were retrieved and ChatGPT produced a factually grounded, sourced response. However, the system struggled with hypothetical 'what if' questions, returning summaries of individual reports rather than synthesised lists of possible consequences. The vector database alone was noted as showing promise for semantic search of incident datasets. Annual costs of approximately $840 for embeddings and database maintenance were identified as a consideration, particularly for smaller organisations.
limitations: Data protection policies prevent use of sensitive or restricted data (e.g., government data, personal details) since data is submitted to a third-party API; ChatGPT can produce hallucinations (incorrect but plausible outputs); ChatGPT generates verbose responses; ChatGPT was only trained on data present up until 2021; The system struggled with hypothetical questions requiring knowledge synthesis beyond the retrieved reports; Risk of over-reliance on the tool in safety-critical settings; Only two closest matching reports were returned, limiting the context provided to ChatGPT; Cost of running the service (~$840/year) represents an additional burden for smaller organisations
research_gaps: Further trials of the concept in actual safety assessment tasks; Creation of bespoke datasets for safety tasks to enable fine-tuning of machine learning models on safety-specific data; Investigation of bespoke LLMs trained on large quantities of safety text to account for unique terminology and context; Returning a greater number of matching reports to provide more context to ChatGPT and improve response quality; Use of alternative data sources such as collections of safety assessment reports or other incident datasets

research_focus: Development of an intelligent enterprise financial risk control system using the Milvus vector database and machine learning to predict enterprise cancellation and revocation risks.
method: The system employs the Milvus vector database for storing and retrieving high-dimensional feature data, combined with random forest classification, Euclidean distance, and cosine similarity for risk assessment and prediction.
application_domain: Enterprise financial risk management and early warning
results_summary: The paper addresses enterprise financial risk prediction by designing a system that integrates the Milvus vector database with machine learning models, specifically random forest, for analyzing and forecasting cancellation and revocation risks. The system leverages Euclidean distance and cosine similarity as similarity measures within the vector database framework to retrieve relevant feature data for risk assessment. The authors claim the system enables real-time analysis, continuous monitoring, and scalable processing of large volumes of enterprise data. The proposed approach is positioned as an improvement over traditional manual risk analysis methods, offering automated, data-driven risk identification and quantification. The paper presents the system as a comprehensive solution for enhancing enterprise risk management precision and supporting strategic decision-making.

research_focus: A comparative analysis of three nearest neighbor search indexing methods—KD-Trees, HNSW, and Product Quantization (PQ)—examining their trade-offs in accuracy, scalability, and memory usage across different dimensionalities and application scenarios.
method: Comparative review of the theoretical foundations, structural mechanisms, limitations, and practical applicability of KD-Trees, HNSW, and PQ, including discussion of the curse of dimensionality and recent improvements such as random rotations and ensembles.
indexing_methods: KD-Tree; HNSW; Product Quantization (PQ); Optimized Product Quantization (OPQ); random rotations; ensembles of KD-Trees
application_domain: Natural language processing, image and video retrieval, recommendation systems, semantic search, geographic information systems (GIS), robotics, and multimedia retrieval
results_summary: The paper systematically compares KD-Trees, HNSW, and PQ for nearest neighbor search, finding that KD-Trees are effective for low-dimensional exact searches (up to ~20 dimensions) but degrade rapidly in higher dimensions due to the curse of dimensionality. HNSW provides high recall with logarithmic complexity for high-dimensional, large-scale datasets but incurs significant memory overhead from multilayer graph connections. PQ offers the best trade-off between compression and accuracy, making it ideal for memory-constrained environments, with OPQ further reducing quantization error. The authors conclude that the optimal choice depends on application-specific requirements including dimensionality, accuracy needs, speed, and memory constraints.
limitations: KD-Trees suffer from the curse of dimensionality, with performance no better than brute-force search beyond ~20 dimensions; KD-Trees require excessive backtracking and inefficient pruning in high-dimensional spaces; HNSW has significant computational cost for graph construction and memory overhead for storing multilayer connections; PQ requires tuning and provides only approximate results rather than exact matches

research_focus: Detecting complex semantic vulnerabilities in smart contracts (specifically AMM price manipulation and initial risk deposit vulnerabilities) by combining vector database retrieval with GPT-based analysis, while reducing token usage costs compared to direct GPT processing.
method: A three-component framework: (1) function signature extraction using solc to generate an abstract syntax tree and vectorize code; (2) vector database storage and retrieval of function implementations; (3) GPT-based iterative vulnerability detection that filters key functions based on common vulnerability scenarios and retrieves relevant implementations for in-depth assessment. Pruning of third-party libraries and interface files is applied before storage.
mentioned_systems: VulnScan GPT; GPTScan; Mythril; Slither; solc; OpenAI
application_domain: Smart contract security and DeFi vulnerability detection on blockchain platforms (Ethereum)
results_summary: VulnScan GPT achieved a precision of 58%, recall of 88%, and F1 score of 70% for AMM price manipulation detection on the Web3bugs dataset, and 70% precision, 90% recall, and 79% F1 on the DefiHacks dataset, slightly outperforming GPTScan. For RFD vulnerabilities, the framework achieved a 67% F1 score, significantly higher than GPTScan's 55%. The framework demonstrated an 89% reduction in token usage compared to submitting entire contracts directly to GPT, with a further 68% reduction after pruning non-essential files. Performance was notably better on the DefiHacks and Top200 datasets than on Web3bugs, attributed to the higher logical complexity of the latter. The authors conclude that the framework provides an efficient and cost-effective solution for detecting complex semantic vulnerabilities that traditional static analysis tools cannot identify.
limitations: Search ambiguity when handling similar function signatures affects detection accuracy; Function segmentation limitations: incorrect segmentation may lead to detection errors, indicating current text processing algorithms need further optimization; Searching based solely on signature similarity has defects when facing similar function signatures; Inaccuracy of GPT in generating function signatures reduces reliability of results; Higher logical complexity in the Web3bugs dataset leads to a significantly higher misclassification rate compared to DefiHacks and Top200; GPTScan comparison on DefiHacks dataset could not be conducted before the submission deadline, so results were based on previously released data
research_gaps: Using regular expressions to build a script to segment Solidity files specifically for smart contract writing habits; Introducing more refined differentiation mechanisms in the vector database search phase to enhance sensitivity to subtle differences between similar function signatures; Developing more effective prompt design and innovative strategies to improve the reliability and accuracy of GPT-generated signatures; Adding natural language descriptions to code blocks as a reference indexing method; Enhancing the framework's robustness against adversarial attacks and ensuring integrity of vector database operations through data validation mechanisms and secure storage technologies; Improving real-time monitoring capabilities by incorporating dynamic data flow analysis and incremental detection techniques; Integrating predictive models for historical vulnerability trend analysis to support identification and prevention of potential risks

research_focus: Comparison of zero-shot prompting and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approaches for text tone classification (sentiment analysis) in the Ukrainian language, evaluated on both binary (positive/negative) and multiclass (positive/neutral/negative) tasks using the Mistral-7B-UK large language model.
method: Two approaches were implemented: (1) zero-shot prompting where prompts describe the role, output format, and tonality explanations for the Mistral-7B-UK model; (2) RAG where Qdrant is used as a vector database and LangChain integrates the LLM with external data sources, retrieving the five most semantically similar chunks to fill prompt templates. Two datasets of Ukrainian-language comments (binary and multiclass) covering reviews of shops, restaurants, hotels, medical facilities, and other services were used for evaluation.
mentioned_systems: Mistral-7B-UK; Qdrant; LangChain; BERT Base Uncased; DistilBERT; XLM-RoBERTa; Ukr-RoBERTa; GPT-3.5; GPT-4; Llama 2; Llama-7B; ChatGPT; LLaMA; SiEBERT; RoBERTa
application_domain: Natural language processing: text tone/sentiment classification of Ukrainian-language customer reviews across multiple domains (shops, restaurants, hotels, medical facilities, entertainment, fitness, services)
results_summary: The paper compared zero-shot prompting and RAG for Ukrainian text tone classification using Mistral-7B-UK. The zero-shot approach achieved higher overall accuracy: 94% for binary classification and 75% for multiclass classification, outperforming RAG by 9% and 4% respectively. The RAG approach showed a particular advantage in recognizing neutral tonality during multiclass classification, where the zero-shot model struggled (correctly classifying only 66 out of 134 neutral comments). However, a key issue with RAG was identified: comments with opposing tonality were retrieved as context because they described the same object (e.g., the same restaurant), which negatively affected classification results. The study concluded that zero-shot prompting is more effective for this task, while RAG's benefit is limited to the neutral category recognition.
limitations: Comments with opposing tonality could be retrieved as context due to a shared object of description, negatively affecting RAG results; The zero-shot model struggles to recognize neutral tonality, misclassifying many neutral comments into other categories; The RAG model has difficulty distinguishing adjacent tonalities, with significant cross-classification between neutral, positive, and negative classes
research_gaps: The effect of RAG on improving results in non-knowledge-intensive tasks, particularly sentiment analysis, still requires further research and experimentation; The challenges associated with multiclass classification, especially in the Ukrainian language, inspire an interest in further study

research_focus: Developing an accessible, AI-driven chatbot (DermAI) for accurate dermatological diagnosis and patient interaction in resource-limited settings, addressing the gap of existing systems that focus on rare/cancerous skin diseases and provide only limited initial diagnoses.
method: Integration of ResNet-50 for skin disease image classification with a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline using AstraDB vector database, OpenAI embedding model, and Chainlit for the conversational interface. A comparative study of five deep learning models (ResNet-50, VGG-19, Inception-V3, MobileNet-V2, EfficientNet-B4) was conducted on a common skin diseases dataset to evaluate and mitigate misclassification.
mentioned_systems: AstraDB; Chainlit; OpenAI; ResNet-50; VGG-19; Inception-V3; MobileNet-V2; EfficientNet-B4; ChatGPT-4o; Model Dermatol; Aysa by Visualdx
application_domain: Dermatology – classification of common skin diseases (melanoma, chickenpox, shingles, impetigo, nail fungus) and patient-facing diagnostic chatbot
results_summary: The paper addresses the need for an accessible, accurate dermatological diagnosis tool by building DermAI, a RAG-based chatbot integrating ResNet-50 image classification with AstraDB vector database and OpenAI embeddings. A comparative study of five deep learning models identified ResNet-50 as the best performer for common skin disease classification. The system achieved a misclassification rate of 2.17%, mean sensitivity of 92.6%, specificity of 99.8%, and AUC of 99.9%, with 100% validation accuracy on melanoma, chickenpox, shingles, impetigo, and nail fungus. The hallucination score averaged 7%, well within the 50% threshold, indicating grounded responses. The authors conclude that DermAI outperforms all previously proposed solutions in the research literature for common skin disease diagnosis.
limitations: Chainlit compatibility conflicts with certain Python modules due to its recent market entry; Chainlit applications are computationally demanding; Chainlit's evolving syntax leads to deprecated code requiring refactoring; Computational demands of deep learning applications with exhaustive image datasets cause performance bottlenecks; Acquiring medical image data is difficult due to privacy concerns and doctor-patient confidentiality; Insufficient images for both training and validation risk underfitting and overfitting; Rouge-2 recall of 35% indicates room for improvement in identifying relevant bigrams; Rouge-L recall of 48% suggests gaps in capturing all relevant information in sequence prediction
research_gaps: Integration of more extensive and diverse dermatological datasets from various sources and populations; Use of cutting-edge computer vision techniques to enhance sensitivity and precision of skin condition detection; Incorporation of multilingual support to cater to a diverse global audience; Improving cultural sensitivity by accounting for regional nuances in expressing and comprehending skin-related issues; Training the model on blurry images to provide accurate diagnosis when users upload low-quality photos; Strategic integration into telemedicine platforms for seamless remote consultations with dermatologists; Integration with electronic health records (EHR) for personalised, medically informed interactions

research_focus: Democratizing enterprise data access through a conversational AI platform (AskDataAI) that combines vector search, role-based access control, and contextual AI to reduce data access bottlenecks and improve decision-making speed across organizational levels.
method: The platform employs specialized AI agents (AskFinance, AskFirefly, AskDataExplorer), Chain-of-Thoughts visualization, mathematical reasoning techniques, and advanced vector search capabilities within a modular architecture with role-based access control.
application_domain: Enterprise data management and analytics for an online food ordering company operating across 27 countries
results_summary: The paper describes the design and deployment of AskDataAI in an online food ordering company processing over 3.5 million delivery orders daily. research_gaps: Optimizing RAG systems in scenarios requiring high-context preservation and precision; Developing more reliable and context-aware RAG systems; Adapting and integrating known retrieval methodologies for real-world information retrieval challenges in additional language domains

research_focus: A comprehensive review of the literature on fine-tuning pre-trained large language models to optimize retrieval processes in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems for domain-specific applications, covering methods such as query optimization, RAFT, RA-DIT, and evaluation frameworks.
method: Literature review covering fine-tuning methodologies (RAFT, RA-DIT, query optimization via reinforcement learning, query expansion, and contrastive learning), evaluation frameworks (RALLE), ensemble approaches combining retrieval-based and generation-based systems, and associated evaluation metrics (precision, recall, F1, BLEU, ROUGE, human judgment).
application_domain: Domain-specific natural language processing, including healthcare (medical terminology), legal, financial, and technical domains, where RAG systems retrieve from vector databases to support LLM response generation.
results_summary: The paper surveys the state-of-the-art in fine-tuning LLMs for RAG systems, comparing approaches such as query optimization, RAFT, RA-DIT, and ensemble methods. It finds that query optimization refines retrieval input, RAFT prepares the generator to handle noisy retrievals via chain-of-thought reasoning, and RA-DIT jointly aligns retriever and generator for improved synergy. The RALLE framework is highlighted as a modular toolset for systematic evaluation of RAG components. The review concludes that combining these complementary methods and developing more sophisticated evaluation frameworks incorporating real-time user feedback are key directions for improving domain-specific RAG performance.
limitations: Non-fine-tuned models struggle to comprehend domain-specific abbreviations and terminology (e.g., 'HTN' for hypertension); Non-fine-tuned models face difficulty maintaining consistency across long conversations or documents; Non-fine-tuned models struggle with ambiguous terms requiring domain-specific disambiguation (e.g., 'BP' as blood pressure vs. British Petroleum); Non-fine-tuned models often fail to incorporate up-to-date information in highly dynamic domains such as legal regulations, medical guidelines, or financial markets; Computational efficiency remains a key challenge for practical real-world deployment of fine-tuned RAG systems
research_gaps: Combining fine-tuning methods (query optimization, RAFT, RA-DIT) more effectively to achieve complementary benefits; Developing more sophisticated evaluation frameworks that incorporate real-time user feedback for continuous adaptation of RAG systems; Exploring the integration of multimodal data sources such as images and structured data to expand RAG applicability in complex environments; Addressing computational efficiency through techniques such as knowledge distillation and model pruning for practical deployment

research_focus: How to securely retrieve company-specific, proprietary information in construction and facility management by augmenting large language models with an external vector-database-backed knowledge base (RAG system).
method: Implementation of a retrieval-augmented generation system using the Mixtral 8x7B model for multilingual text processing and the Milvus vector database for document storage and retrieval, evaluated with quantitative metrics (ROUGE, BLEU, semantic similarity) and qualitative human-like assessments on a dataset of construction-related documents.
application_domain: Construction and facility management, including retrieval from operation manuals, inspection results, blueprints, technical drawings, and Building Information Modeling (BIM) data
results_summary: The authors designed and implemented a RAG system exclusively with open-source components to allow secure on-premises deployment, then evaluated it on 30 facility-management question-answer pairs using both automated and human-like metrics. limitations: Notable challenges in maintaining lexical precision and factual accuracy of generated answers; Restriction to PDF files, limiting the system's ability to handle heterogeneous file types encountered in construction projects; Need for further refinement of the retrieval and generation processes to enhance overall performance and reliability

research_focus: A structured review and taxonomy of traditional file similarity digests (ssdeep, sdhash, TLSH) and modern approaches (embeddings, vector databases) for scalable malware detection and file similarity search in enterprise environments.
method: The paper classifies and compares different similarity digest algorithms, similarity search and clustering strategies, and vector database solutions. It proposes an integrated approach combining TLSH with off-the-shelf vector databases to bypass custom implementations like HAC-T, and provides a structured taxonomy of methods.
mentioned_systems: Milvus; Pinecone; Weaviate; NSRL; MalwareBazaar; YARA; HAC-T
indexing_methods: HNSW; ANNOY; LSH; Bloom filter trees
application_domain: Malware detection, threat hunting, and digital forensics in enterprise cybersecurity
results_summary: The paper provides a structured taxonomy comparing traditional similarity digests (ssdeep, sdhash, TLSH) with modern embedding-based and vector database approaches for malware variant detection. It highlights that traditional exact-match systems are ill-suited for similarity digests and that brute-force comparison is computationally expensive at enterprise scale. The authors propose combining TLSH with off-the-shelf vector databases (e.g., Milvus, Pinecone, Weaviate) as an optimal approach that avoids custom clustering implementations like HAC-T. The survey emphasizes that a layered detection strategy combining fuzzy digests with machine learning and vector database technologies is necessary for robust, real-time detection across massive datasets.
limitations: Traditional exact-match systems (key-value stores, relational databases) are not well-suited for storing and retrieving similarity digests; Brute-force comparison of similarity digests is computationally expensive; Different similarity techniques encode information in different ways, making it difficult to design a common data structure across techniques; Existing clustering methods (HAC-T for TLSH, Bloom filter trees for sdhash) struggle to generalize well across different datasets or are challenging to implement in practice; Static feeds of indicators of compromise are cumbersome to maintain and update; Cryptographic hashes drastically change with minor modifications, enabling malware authors to evade detection
research_gaps: Developing more versatile clustering frameworks that balance scalability, ease of use, and precision; Hybrid clustering methods incorporating density-based or centroid-based clustering with domain-specific optimizations; Stronger integration between language models and malware analysis; Further research and development in combining traditional digests with modern vector database solutions for scalable detection

research_gaps: Continued exploration and refinement of vector search techniques; Further development of technologies that will shape the direction of data retrieval systems

research_focus: Creating a document search framework that uses vector-based approaches to retrieve specific information from large collections of documents (especially PDFs), making search simple, fast, and accessible.
method: Document content is preprocessed (stop word removal, tokenization, normalization), vectorized using state-of-the-art vectorization techniques, stored in a vector database (MilvusDB), and retrieved via cosine similarity search.
application_domain: Document search and information retrieval over PDF files and books
results_summary: The paper presents a document search system that vectorizes document content and stores the resulting vectors in MilvusDB for similarity-based retrieval. Documents are preprocessed through stop word removal, tokenization, and normalization before vectorization. research_focus: Developing a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) chatbot to improve access to Mauritian legal information for both legal professionals and non-professionals, addressing the difficulty of navigating over 1200 pieces of legislation in a hybrid legal system.
method: A RAG system was built by chunking 46 legal documents (acts and regulations) and storing them as vectors in Chroma. Queries are processed by an LLM (GPT-4o-mini or MistralAI Open-Mixtral-8x22B) that performs similarity searches against the vector database and generates grounded responses. A translation layer handles French queries, and a re-ranking algorithm selects the most appropriate retrieved documents. The chunking overlap parameter was tuned to 200 to improve context per chunk.
mentioned_systems: Chroma; OpenAI GPT-4o-mini; MistralAI Open-Mixtral-8x22B; lawanswers.me
application_domain: Legal information retrieval and legal question-answering in the Mauritian legal sector
results_summary: The RAG chatbot was evaluated through a User Acceptance Test by a legal professional, a final-year LLB student, and a non-technical Mauritian citizen. Both LLMs provided correct or relevant responses in most of the 20 test questions, though some answers were incomplete (e.g., missing references to the Code Civil or the right to be accompanied). The Mistral AI model (open-mixtral-8x22b) consistently outperformed GPT-4o-mini on French-language queries and produced more detailed, structured answers on topics such as company secretary duties and workers' rights. The legal professional found the system satisfactory and useful for improving access to justice, while the non-technical user found it very user-friendly and helpful.
limitations: Heavy reliance on the quality and completeness of the legal documents made available to the system; Some queries produced incomplete answers, such as omitting the right to be accompanied or references to the Code Civil and DPA; Initial testing showed many questions were not properly answered, requiring finetuning of the chunking overlap parameter

research_focus: Enhancing the emotional and contextual understanding of large language models in psychiatric/psychotherapy applications through a novel Emotion-Aware Embedding Fusion framework that integrates hierarchical fusion and attention mechanisms.
method: Therapy transcripts are segmented into word-, sentence-, and session-level representations using neural networks. Hierarchical fusion with pooling techniques combines these levels, while multi-head self-attention and cross-attention prioritize emotionally salient features. Emotion lexicons (NRC, VADER, WordNet, SentiWordNet) enrich the embeddings, which are computed using BERT, GPT-3, and RoBERTa, stored in a FAISS vector database for similarity search, and retrieved as context for LLMs (Flan-T5, Llama 2, DeepSeek-R1, ChatGPT 4) to generate empathetic responses.

application_domain: AI-driven psychotherapy, mental health chatbots, crisis intervention, and hybrid AI-therapist collaboration in clinical settings
results_summary: The Emotion-Aware Embedding Fusion framework was evaluated across multiple practical use cases including AI-driven therapy chatbots, with assessments spanning Attention Weight Analysis, Temporal Emotion Shifts Evaluation, and Contextual Relevance Analysis. The framework demonstrated significant improvements in empathy, coherence, informativeness, and fluency compared to baseline LLMs (Flan-T5, Llama 2, DeepSeek-R1, ChatGPT 4). It outperformed standard RAG by producing emotionally attuned responses while maintaining logical consistency, thanks to hierarchical embedding fusion and emotion-aware lexicon integration. The comparative analysis showed that BERT excels in emotion detection while DeepSeek-R1 and GPT-4 excel in coherent response generation, and the combined approach balanced both capabilities. The framework was shown to be integrable into existing mental health platforms such as Woebot and Wysa for personalized, contextually relevant therapy responses.

method: Conceptual framework that categorizes database roles into three context types—conversational context (key-value/document databases), situational context (relational databases/data lakehouses), and semantic context (vector databases)—and discusses how a multi-database approach enriches AI-generated responses.
application_domain: Generative AI applications broadly, with examples in healthcare, finance, customer support, and software development
results_summary: The paper proposes a three-context framework (conversational, situational, semantic) to map database types to their respective roles in GenAI workflows. The authors conclude that a multi-database approach combining relational, document, and vector databases allows GenAI applications to deliver more context-aware, personalized, and high-performing responses. The paper emphasizes that database selection directly impacts model efficiency, scalability, and the quality of AI-generated outputs.

research_focus: The paper addresses the security vulnerabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs), specifically injection attacks, hallucinations, and data privacy breaches, by proposing a multi-layered security framework that integrates VectorDB, Kernel, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) within a cross-LLM architecture.
method: The proposed system employs a pipeline consisting of injection detection and elimination using transformer-based models, core processing supported by a Vector Database (Pinecone VectorDB) and RAG modules for semantic vector representation and context filtering, and a cross-LLM validation stage with an eligibility score (EC) mechanism that cross-validates responses across multiple LLMs (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4o, Gemini, PaLM, Llama) to determine publishability.
mentioned_systems: Pinecone VectorDB; VectorDB; RAG; Kernel; MART; SIEM; PaLM; Llama; GPT-3.5; GPT-4; GPT-4o; Gemini
application_domain: LLM security and NLP, specifically for detecting and mitigating prompt injection attacks, hallucinations, and bias in large language model responses, with applications in cybersecurity, multilingual processing, and adaptive threat detection.
results_summary: The paper introduces a security framework combining VectorDB, Kernel, and RAG within a cross-LLM architecture to protect LLMs against injection attacks and hallucinations. The system was evaluated across multiple LLMs (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4o, Gemini, PaLM, Llama) and achieved 98% accuracy in eligibility scoring. Experimental results across eight adversarial scenarios demonstrated that the system outperforms conventional LLMs in detecting manipulative queries, enforcing language restrictions, and blocking sensitive information requests. The cross-LLM validation with eligibility score control effectively filtered unsafe or incorrect responses that base LLMs would otherwise publish. The authors conclude that the multi-layered defense mechanism provides a more robust and scalable security solution compared to prompt-only or single-model approaches.
research_gaps: Reinforcing defenses against additional manipulation types; Expanding multi-language support; Further optimizing collaboration among diverse LLM models; Recognizing additional manipulation types beyond those currently handled

research_focus: Automated security test case generation for APIs targeting Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA) vulnerabilities, using LLMs combined with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) techniques and Karate DSL.
method: A modular framework (Karate-BOLA-Guard) integrating multiple LLM models (Llama 3 8B, Phi-3 Mini, Mistral) with RAG-enhanced context retrieval via vector databases, iterative self-improving test case generation in Karate DSL, and observability tools for process monitoring. Evaluation was conducted on three deliberately vulnerable APIs and fifteen production APIs across diverse domains.
mentioned_systems: Karate-BOLA-Guard; Karate DSL; VAmPI; Crapi; OWASP Juice Shop; Llama 3 8B; Phi-3 Mini; Mistral; APIRank
application_domain: API security testing, specifically BOLA vulnerability detection across social media, version control, financial services, and transportation APIs
results_summary: The paper introduced Karate-BOLA-Guard, a framework combining LLMs and RAG for automated BOLA vulnerability test generation, and evaluated it on three vulnerable APIs and fifteen production APIs. Llama 3 8B achieved consistent performance with Accuracy scores of 3.1-3.4 and Interoperability of 3.7-4.3, with an average processing time of 143.76 seconds on GPU. GPU acceleration yielded 20-25x improvement over CPU, while smaller models (Phi-3 Mini, Mistral) processed faster at 69.58 and 72.14 seconds respectively. Performance varied across APIs, with notably strong results on complex platforms like Instagram (A=4.3, I=4.4) and consistent functionality on simpler implementations like VAmPI (A=3.6, I=4.3). The iterative refinement process demonstrated that RAG-enhanced, LLM-driven approaches can provide targeted, context-aware security test generation beyond brute-force methods.
limitations: Performance gap between models suggests larger, more resource-intensive models may be necessary for optimal results; Specific configuration choices (context window size of 1000 tokens, temperature of 0.3) and hardware variations between CPU and GPU could limit deployment in resource-constrained environments and real-time applications; The approach may not capture all possible vulnerability scenarios, particularly those requiring complex multi-step interactions; Primary focus on BOLA vulnerabilities may limit effectiveness in detecting other types of API security vulnerabilities; Variability in performance across different LLMs introduces inconsistencies in test generation and affects framework reliability; Results may not generalize to all API types, particularly those with unique authentication mechanisms or complex business logic; Potential for generating tests that incorrectly identify non-existent vulnerabilities (false positives) needs further investigation; Evaluation metrics (Accuracy, Interoperability, Complexity) might not capture all relevant aspects of test case quality and effectiveness
research_gaps: Need for more sophisticated test generation strategies to handle complex, multi-step vulnerability interactions; Further investigation and mitigation strategies for false positives in generated test cases; Further validation of framework performance on diverse real-world APIs with varying complexity and unique authentication mechanisms

research_focus: Developing a cryptocurrency security expert system that leverages local LLMs, embeddings, and vector databases for symmetry-based anomaly detection and threat identification in cryptocurrency transactions.
method: A modular framework integrating a local LLM, embedding-based data representation, and ChromaDB vector database via LangChain, using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and symmetry-aware analysis of transaction patterns for real-time anomaly detection.
mentioned_systems: Chroma DB; LangChain; BERT; GPT-4; LLaMA
application_domain: Cryptocurrency and blockchain security, including phishing detection, fraudulent transaction identification, and blockchain anomaly detection
results_summary: The proposed expert system was evaluated on a benchmark dataset of cryptocurrency transactions including real-world threat scenarios (phishing, fraudulent transactions, blockchain anomalies). The system achieved 92% accuracy, 89% precision, and 93% recall, representing a 10% improvement over existing security frameworks. Compared to traditional rule-based and machine learning-based detection methods, the approach significantly enhanced real-time threat detection while reducing false positives. The integration of LLMs with embeddings and vector retrieval enabled more efficient contextual anomaly detection, with a reported latency reduction of up to 50% compared to conventional models.
limitations: Computational costs remain a critical challenge for deployment; Data handling complexities limit practical scalability; Scalability issues as transaction volumes and threat sophistication continue to grow; The dynamic nature of cyber threats necessitates continuous adaptation and enhancement of models
research_gaps: Developing more efficient, self-updating models that can dynamically adapt to new security challenges; Implementing continuous learning to counter emerging attack vectors; Adoption of advanced LLMs for improved performance; Addressing scalability as transaction volumes and threat sophistication continue to grow

research_focus: Development and implementation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-based chatbot system that integrates LLMs with a FAISS vector database to improve information retrieval and response accuracy for college-specific queries, addressing data insufficiency and static knowledge limitations of LLMs.
method: The system uses Beautiful Soup for web scraping college websites to collect data (course offers, faculty biographies, admissions details), vectorizes text into dense embeddings stored in FAISS for nearest-neighbor similarity search, and integrates LLMs (LLaMA, Gemini, Groq AI) within a RAG framework to generate contextually appropriate natural-language responses. A Streamlit interface is used for user interaction, and Groq AI is employed to reduce response time.
mentioned_systems: FAISS; LLaMA; Gemini; Groq AI; Streamlit; Beautiful Soup; ChatGPT
application_domain: College and academic information retrieval (course details, admissions procedures, faculty information)
results_summary: The paper presents the design and implementation of a RAG-based chatbot that combines FAISS vector search with LLMs (LLaMA, Gemini, Groq AI) to answer college-specific queries from scraped web data and PDF documents containing text and embedded images. The system vectorizes text into dense embeddings, retrieves relevant passages via FAISS nearest-neighbor search, and passes them to an LLM for contextually accurate response generation. The authors report that the integrated approach improves user engagement in academic settings, automates institutional communication, and reduces human labor compared to traditional chatbots. The system also handles image-related information within PDFs, which traditional chatbots struggle to extract. The authors conclude that the fusion of LLMs, FAISS-based vector retrieval, and the RAG framework provides a scalable and intelligent solution for educational institutions.
limitations: LLMs are inherently limited by their dependence on static knowledge, real-time flexibility, and input size restrictions; Traditional chatbots struggle with extracting meaning from visual data in documents
research_gaps: Advanced image analysis with deep learning; Domain-specific fine-tuning for academic inquiries; Multilingual support to assist a diverse student body; Knowledge graph integration to enhance factual accuracy; Deployment as a cloud-based solution to improve accessibility and scalability

research_focus: Integration of embedding vector databases into Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems through a hybrid retrieval architecture that combines dense vector search with traditional keyword-based methods to overcome limitations of standalone LLMs such as knowledge cutoff, hallucinations, and lack of domain-specific access.
method: A modular RAG architecture with a dual-encoder retriever (BERT-based, 768-dimensional embeddings, contrastive learning with hard negative mining) and a sequence-to-sequence generator, combined with a novel rank fusion algorithm that dynamically integrates dense vector retrieval and BM25 lexical retrieval using query-dependent weighting. The system was evaluated across multiple vector database technologies and document collection scales using precision@k, recall@k, MAP, and NDCG metrics.
mentioned_systems: Pinecone; Weaviate; Milvus; Qdrant; BERT; Sentence Transformers
application_domain: NLP and information retrieval for LLM augmentation; specific application domains include healthcare, legal services, and technical support
results_summary: The paper proposes and implements a hybrid retrieval RAG architecture that integrates embedding vector databases with traditional keyword-based retrieval. Experimental results show the hybrid approach achieves 30-35% recall improvement over keyword-only (BM25) methods and 15-20% over pure vector search on standard information retrieval benchmarks. The system reduces hallucinations by up to 30% compared to standalone LLMs while maintaining sub-100ms query response times in optimized implementations. Performance was benchmarked across Pinecone, Weaviate, and Milvus at varying document collection scales. Domain-adapted RAG implementations demonstrated substantial improvements over general-purpose systems, particularly in healthcare and legal domains.
limitations: Standalone LLMs suffer from knowledge cutoff limitations, hallucination tendencies, and inability to access domain-specific or proprietary information; Retrieval performance degrades in both accuracy and latency as document collections scale to enterprise levels; Vector databases can be memory-intensive, particularly for large datasets; Embedding-based retrieval struggles with exact matching of rare terms or specific factual details; Lexical methods (e.g. BM25) miss semantically related content; Different vector database solutions offer varying tradeoffs between query speed, storage efficiency, and accuracy, complicating implementation selection
research_gaps: As LLMs continue to evolve, hybrid RAG approaches will need to play an increasingly vital role in grounding models with external knowledge for real-world applications demanding accuracy and contextual relevance; Tailored system design based on specific application requirements and domain characteristics is needed rather than generic solutions

research_focus: Development and evaluation of a RAG-based chatbot (Thyro-GenAI) for personalized thyroid disease management, comparing its ability to generate patient-personalized clinical reasoning output against existing service LLMs.
method: A RAG-based chatbot was developed by integrating a vector database of thyroid disease textbooks and guidelines with an LLM. Thyro-GenAI and three service LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, Perplexity AI's ChatGPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet) were asked personalized clinical questions about thyroid disease, and three thyroid specialists assessed the quality of generated responses and references using inverse-weighted mean rank scoring.
mentioned_systems: Thyro-GenAI; ChatGPT-4o; Perplexity AI; Claude 3.5 Sonnet
application_domain: Thyroid disease clinical decision support and patient management in endocrinology
results_summary: Thyro-GenAI achieved the highest inverse-weighted mean rank for overall response quality (3.0) compared to ChatGPT (2.3), Perplexity (2.8), and Claude (1.9), and the second-highest rank for reference quality (3.1). Evaluators confirmed that by utilizing a vector database, Thyro-GenAI produced reliable, patient-specific clinical reasoning responses with fewer hallucinations. In contrast, the other LLMs were criticized for frequently omitting critical information or including unnecessary or inaccurate details. Thyro-GenAI was ranked second to Perplexity in reference relevance, attributed to the limited comprehensiveness of its database of infrequently updated textbooks and guidelines. Overall, the RAG-based approach demonstrated enhanced safety and clinical applicability compared to standalone service LLMs.
limitations: Evaluation relied on human graders, introducing potential bias; Small number of evaluators (N = 3); Thyro-GenAI is hosted on a cloud platform, making it difficult to use in environments with unstable or limited internet connections; No ablation analysis was conducted to isolate the specific contribution of RAG technology; RAG systems exhibit limitations in semantic comprehension of complex medical ontologies and intricate reasoning pathway relationships; Limited comprehensiveness of the database, as textbooks and guidelines were infrequently updated; Occasional inaccuracies and hallucinations caused by limited datasets

research_focus: Developing a cost-effective, low-latency end-to-end Natural Language to SQL (NL2SQL) pipeline for enterprise database analytics that minimizes LLM costs while maintaining accuracy, addressing the gap where existing methods overlook enterprise cost, latency, and overall analytical search experience.
method: An end-to-end pipeline (ASKSQL) combining an intelligent schema selector (encoder-based model), an adapter-based (QLoRA) fine-tuned PLM for SQL generation, a self-ranking SQL correction module, an ANN-index-based query recommendation with entity-swapping, and an association graph-based semantic caching network to reduce LLM calls by leveraging semantically similar historical queries.
application_domain: Enterprise database analytics and natural language to SQL query generation, with a focus on the finance domain
results_summary: The paper presents the ASKSQL pipeline, an end-to-end NL2SQL system integrating schema selection, adapter-based query generation, semantic caching, and entity swapping to reduce LLM costs and latency in enterprise settings. Experimental results demonstrate an average accuracy increase of 5.83% and an overall latency decrease of 32.6% as the usage count of the pipeline increases. The pipeline's performance improves over time as it adapts to new queries and search patterns. The system is shown to be cost-efficient and suitable for enterprise environments where query repetition and similarity are prevalent.
limitations: Suffers from large-scale domain analytics where search queries span different domains due to the use of small language models; The semantic caching component is finance-tuned, limiting cross-domain applicability; Fine-tuned PLMs are unable to generalize well to unseen data or handle complex queries involving inner joins and nested SQL structures
research_gaps: Extending the caching mechanism and domain expansion from finance to the general domain as a plugin; Introducing more resilient recommendations to improve pipeline performance across various domains

research_focus: How iterative reset strategies applied to key components of a RAG pipeline (vector database, stylistic analysis, keyword extraction, retrieval queries) can enhance text summarization quality, specifically improving content overlap, summary coherence, and reducing retrieval noise.
method: A RAG pipeline combining text segmentation, semantic embedding, vector database indexing, keyword extraction, and stylistic analysis was developed. Five discrete reset strategies were implemented and iteratively evaluated on the eLife dataset, with performance measured using ROUGE-1/2/L, FactCC, Flesch-Kincaid readability scores, and processing time, compared against six baseline models.
application_domain: Text summarization of scientific literature (eLife dataset), natural language processing
results_summary: The paper evaluated five iterative reset strategies within a RAG-based summarization pipeline on the eLife dataset. Method 3 (Vector Database Reset) and Method 5 (Full Reset) achieved the highest ROUGE-1 scores (0.3716 and 0.3706) and showed lower standard deviations in R-1 scores, indicating more consistent content overlap across iterations. However, their FactCC scores (0.1263 and 0.1186) remained moderate compared to GPT-4o mini (0.242), revealing that gains in content overlap did not fully translate to factual accuracy. Reset strategies also incurred substantially higher processing times (over 1300 seconds for Methods 4 and 5 versus 246 seconds for the baseline), highlighting an efficiency trade-off. Overall, iterative resets improved summarization coherence and reduced retrieval noise but introduced challenges in maintaining factual consistency.
limitations: Exclusive reliance on the eLife dataset, which may affect generalizability of findings; Limited set of comparison models used for evaluation; Reset strategies incur substantially higher processing times compared to the baseline; Variable factual consistency (FactCC) despite improved ROUGE scores
research_gaps: Exploration of adaptive reset mechanisms that more effectively harmonize retrieval refinement with factual verification; Expanding evaluations to include diverse datasets beyond eLife; Incorporating human assessments to further refine and validate the methods

research_focus: Automating medical ontology mapping for RDF knowledge graph construction using Large Language Models, specifically comparing six systems for mapping medical terms to the SNOMED CT ontology.
method: A data preprocessing pipeline (terminology normalization, abbreviation expansion, unit standardization) combined with an LLM-powered semantic mapping engine that uses BioBERT embeddings stored in ChromaDB for concept retrieval via cosine similarity. A novel evaluation framework combining quantitative metrics (precision, recall, F-score) with qualitative assessments of semantic accuracy was applied to a dataset of 108 expert-validated medical terms.
mentioned_systems: GPT-4o; Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2; Gemini 1.5 Pro; Llama 3.3 70B; DeepSeek R1; BERTMap; ChromaDB; BioBERT
application_domain: Medical ontology mapping and RDF knowledge graph construction (SNOMED CT)
results_summary: The paper conducted a comparative evaluation of six systems for mapping 108 medical terms to the SNOMED CT ontology, using a combined quantitative and qualitative evaluation framework. GPT-4o achieved the highest performance with 93.75% precision, 98.90% recall, and 96.26% F-score, substantially outperforming all other systems. The performance hierarchy was: GPT-4o > Gemini 1.5 Pro (63.31% F1) > Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 (60.56% F1) > BERTMap (57.93% F1) > Llama 3.3 70B (30.16% F1) > DeepSeek R1 (28.81% F1). A chi-square test confirmed statistically significant differences between methods (p < 0.001, Cramer's V = 0.32). Error analysis showed that all systems struggled with complex quantitative measurements and multi-parameter clinical assessments, with smaller open-source models exhibiting particularly high false positive rates.
limitations: Performance variability depends on training data quality and coverage, with rare or highly specialized concepts presenting challenges for all methods; GPT-4o's few misclassifications were concentrated in complex quantitative measurements, multi-parameter clinical assessments, and certain anatomical treatment locations; The need for domain expert validation remains, particularly for critical applications; GPT-4o's high computational demands and cost may limit its feasibility for certain applications; The dataset of 108 medical terms, while expert-validated, is limited in size and may not fully capture the breadth of medical terminology

research_focus: Improving the efficiency of feature matching in image matching by replacing exhaustive nearest neighbor search in descriptor space with a hierarchical, group-based approach that first matches clusters of spatial features and then individual features within those clusters.
method: A hierarchical pipeline (GGNN) that employs hyperdimensional computing for efficient group testing of feature similarities. The approach first detects, describes, and matches feature groups (clusters of spatial features) rather than directly matching individual features, and subsequently matches individual features within the matched groups.
indexing_methods: exact nearest neighbor search; approximate nearest neighbor search; FLANN; hyperdimensional computing
application_domain: Image matching for image stitching, 3D reconstruction, and simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM)
results_summary: The paper proposes GGNN, a hierarchical group-guided nearest neighbor approach that circumvents exhaustive NN search in descriptor space by first matching clusters of spatial features and then individual features within those matched clusters. The method leverages spatial relationships between features and uses hyperdimensional computing for efficient group testing of feature similarities. Experimental evidence suggests that this group-based approach is both efficient and highly effective for image matching. The approach addresses the 'leaky abstraction' problem where identifying the most similar features does not necessarily yield geometrically meaningful matches, particularly in images with repetitive patterns.

research_focus: Improving vector embeddings of scientific text in biomedical domains by combining contrastive learning with a Mixture of Experts (MoE) extension on pretrained BERT models, using co-citation as a similarity metric to train discriminative representations.
method: A novel MoE extension pipeline in which every multi-layer perceptron section of a pretrained BERT model is copied into distinct experts, combined with contrastive learning via a custom MNR variant. Domain-specific datasets are assembled using co-citations as a similarity metric across multiple biological domains. A special-token-based routing scheme ensures the MoE system has the same throughput as a regular transformer.
mentioned_systems: BERT; ModernBERT; SciBERT; PubmedBERT; BioBERT; RoBERTa; Llama-3.2; MPnet; E5; MiniLM
application_domain: Biomedical scientific literature search and vector database compilation, covering domains including skin cancer, COPD, cardiovascular disease, parasitic diseases, and autoimmune diseases.
results_summary: The full MoE approach with contrastive learning (MoEall) achieved the highest average F1max of 0.8875 across all biomedical domains. Single-expert models fine-tuned for a specific domain performed best in most domains (skin cancer, COPD, CVD, parasitic), except in the autoimmune domain where MoEall narrowly outperformed the single-expert variant. The MoE extension increased average separation of co-cited papers in vector space, as reflected in higher vector ratio metrics. However, in the CVD domain, MoEall and SEall failed to outperform base sentence similarity models, with only the domain-specific SEcvd model surpassing them. The SEall model without MoE extension also performed nearly on par with MoEall, suggesting the strong base model (ModernBERT) reduced the relative benefit of the MoE extension.
limitations: MoEall and SEall failed to outperform base sentence similarity models on CVD abstracts, where only the domain-specific SEcvd model achieved better performance; The MoE extension had a smaller performance effect with the ModernBERT base model compared to previous experiments using SciBERT, reducing the relative advantage of the MoE approach
research_gaps: Developing versatile and efficient One-Size-Fits-All transformer networks for encoding heterogeneous biomedical inputs; Enhancing vector database search and compilation using the improved embeddings
