research_focus: The paper addresses the challenge of automating smart home device orchestration by proposing a framework that combines generative AI (LLMs), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with vector databases, and the OSGi modular framework to enable natural language-driven, dynamic service bundle generation and real-time deployment.
method: The system uses LLMs enhanced with RAG to interpret natural language user requests and generate executable Java-based service bundles, with contextual knowledge retrieved from vector databases. Generated bundles are dynamically deployed via the OSGi framework (Apache Felix service registry), with device registration handled through MQTT announcements. A two-tiered data storage strategy combining vector and relational databases supports semantic search for capturing user intent.
application_domain: Smart home automation and IoT device orchestration, where vector search is used to retrieve contextual knowledge for LLM-based code generation of service bundles
results_summary: The proposed orchestrator was validated through multiple use-case scenarios covering dynamic device discovery, on-demand code generation, and adaptive orchestration based on user preferences. Results demonstrated high scalability, with the OSGi framework and Apache Felix service registry accommodating an expanding number of devices without noticeable performance degradation. Extensibility was confirmed through dynamic device registration via MQTT and runtime installation of OSGi bundles, while adaptability was shown by translating natural language requests into executable Java service bundles without a full system restart. Reliability was maintained throughout rigorous testing, with the orchestrator consistently executing automation tasks without failures even under rapid device additions or unexpected user inputs. The system outperformed conventional rule-based approaches by enabling autonomous, real-time generation and deployment of service logic in response to evolving user demands.
limitations: Code generation relies on a general-purpose language model rather than a domain-specific one, potentially reducing accuracy for complex smart home requests; The system requires discrete bundle installations for each automation change rather than supporting live updates or inter-bundle communication; The orchestrator is limited to the Java/OSGi ecosystem and does not support broader IoT platforms
research_gaps: Training domain-specific LLMs on smart home or OSGi service patterns to increase precision and reduce manual oversight in code generation; Implementing dynamic bundle updates and inter-bundle communication mechanisms to enhance responsiveness; Extending support to device ecosystems beyond Java/OSGi through interoperable APIs or language-agnostic interfaces; Developing verification strategies such as static analysis or model checking to detect logical errors or security vulnerabilities in automatically generated code before deployment

research_focus: Generating character-consistent and personalized dialogue for Non-Player Characters (NPCs) in Role-Playing Games, addressing the challenges of limited memory retention, inconsistent character representation, and 'character hallucination' in LLM-based dialogue systems.
method: A framework combining protective static knowledge fine-tuning to constrain LLM output within character scope, a dynamic knowledge graph for short-term memory, a vector database for long-term memory retrieval, AMR (Abstract Meaning Representation) parsing for player intent understanding, and a graph neural network to encode a fused AMR-KG graph into high-dimensional semantic vectors for vector-database retrieval.
mentioned_systems: BART; LLaMA; Alpaca 7B; Vicuna 7B; ChatGPT; GPT-2; LoRA
application_domain: Role-playing game NPC dialogue generation and interactive storytelling
results_summary: The paper proposes a framework that integrates protective static knowledge fine-tuning, dynamic knowledge graphs, AMR parsing, and vector-database retrieval to generate character-consistent NPC dialogues. Experimental results demonstrate that the framework significantly enhances the authenticity of NPC dialogues and player immersion across multiple large language models (BART, LLaMA, Alpaca 7B, Vicuna 7B, ChatGPT), validating its universality and scalability. Ablation experiments confirm the individual effectiveness of the AMR parsing, knowledge graph fusion, and graph pruning modules. research_focus: Identifying multiple types of unknown IoT devices simultaneously in open environments, where existing methods can only identify one type at a time with relatively low accuracy and struggle to adapt to evolving device populations.
method: A CSCL-Siamese network trained with cost-sensitive contrastive loss on permutation positive-negative sample pairs is used to identify known IoT devices and build an embedded vector database. Embedding vectors of unknown devices are extracted and checked against this database. A weighted-voting clustering ensemble (WVE) then integrates multiple unsupervised clustering algorithms to cluster the unknown-device embedding vectors and identify their types.
application_domain: IoT device identification and network security (cross-network attack detection, IoT-botnet detection, network-attack traceability)
results_summary: The paper proposes the CSCL-WVE-UDI method, which combines a cost-sensitive contrastive loss Siamese network with a weighted-voting clustering ensemble to identify multiple types of unknown IoT devices simultaneously. The method was evaluated on benchmark datasets (Aalto, UNSW, LSIF) and compared with prior approaches. Experimental results demonstrate that the method can effectively identify multiple types of unknown IoT devices at the same time, validated by identifying three randomly selected unknown IoT devices. The approach overcomes the limitation of prior methods that could only distinguish one unknown device type per attempt or required prior knowledge of the number of unknown devices.
limitations: The Siamese network can only process a single fingerprint feature because only grayscale images are used to construct device fingerprints; The CSCL-Siamese network requires a considerable number of known IoT devices for training before unknown device identification can proceed
research_gaps: Combining image data with other fingerprint features to form a new, unified IoT device fingerprint; Developing methods for identifying unknown IoT devices that do not rely on data from known IoT devices

research_focus: Designing a full in-memory Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search (ANNS) system on CXL memory devices to overcome memory bandwidth and data movement bottlenecks for billion-scale vector search in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines.
method: COSMOS integrates programmable general-purpose cores (GPCs) in CXL memory controllers for full ANNS offload, exploits DRAM rank-level parallelism for concurrent distance computation, and uses an adjacency-aware data placement algorithm based on cluster metadata to balance search loads across CXL devices without runtime profiling.
application_domain: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for Large Language Models
results_summary: COSMOS was evaluated on SIFT1B and DEEP1B traces against a baseline CXL system and a state-of-the-art CXL-based solution (CXL-ANNS). COSMOS achieves up to 6.72× higher throughput than the baseline and 2.35× over CXL-ANNS, demonstrating significant scalability for RAG pipelines. The adjacency-aware data placement algorithm consistently produces a lower load imbalance ratio compared to round-robin distribution across varying probe counts. The system significantly reduces both graph traversal and distance calculation latency by combining in-memory execution with rank-level parallelism, eliminating host intervention during search.

research_focus: Improving RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) performance for structured tabular data by proposing a hierarchical node-based header representation that reorganizes table information to enhance retrieval accuracy.
method: The paper classifies tables into four types based on structural complexity and domain-knowledge requirements, transposes table data when critical information resides in indices, and encodes domain-specific knowledge as hierarchical nodes in table headers. Retrieval is evaluated using a DTC (Distributed Table Collection) versus UCC (Unified Context Collection) vector database structure, with experiments varying the embedding model (ADA-002) and LLM (GPT-3.5).
application_domain: Retrieval-augmented generation for structured tabular data in business intelligence and domain-specific knowledge retrieval (e.g., finance)
results_summary: The proposed hierarchical node-based header representation consistently outperformed the untransformed baseline across all four table types (I–IV). The DTC vector database structure yielded higher accuracy than the UCC structure regardless of whether data were transposed. For complex tables requiring domain-specific knowledge (Types III and IV), transposing data and converting index information into hierarchical nodes designated as headers produced the highest retrieval accuracy. The method surpassed even approaches that incorporated all table values, providing empirical support for the hypothesis that headers are a key factor in table-retrieval performance. Results were robust across variations in embedding models and LLMs.
limitations: The dataset used in the study was relatively small; Further validation is necessary to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method on larger-scale datasets
research_gaps: Developing techniques for automatically identifying table headers in large-scale datasets; Analyzing how the relationship between short text passages associated with tables and their headers can enhance RAG performance

research_focus: Building a Transformer-based Legal Information Retrieval System for the Indian legal domain that overcomes the limitations of traditional keyword-based search by leveraging semantic understanding, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and explainable AI to retrieve relevant statutes and case judgments.
method: The system integrates the Gemma 2B-IT instruction-tuned language model with LlamaIndex for a RAG pipeline, using all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sentence-transformer embeddings for dense vector indexing and similarity matching over a curated corpus of 50 Indian legal acts and over 4,000 case judgments. GPU-accelerated embeddings and 4-bit quantized inference are employed for real-time performance, and explainability features (attention visualization, citation tracking, document highlighting) are incorporated.
application_domain: Legal information retrieval (Indian statutes, case judgments, and judicial rulings across domains such as RTI, environmental law, labor regulations, and anti-corruption law)
results_summary: The proposed system was evaluated on a corpus of 50 Indian legal acts and over 4,000 case judgments using both quantitative metrics (precision, recall, response time) and qualitative user feedback from law students, faculty, and practicing advocates. Compared to TF-IDF and BM25 baselines, the system demonstrated substantial gains in semantic understanding and contextual alignment, achieving 85-92% accuracy/relevance versus 60-70% for existing systems. Average response time was approximately 620 ms thanks to GPU-accelerated embeddings and 4-bit quantized inference. User satisfaction reached 88% (versus 65% for existing tools), and the explainability features (embedded citations, structured section identifiers, document highlights) were reported to significantly improve user confidence and reduce manual verification time.
research_gaps: Extending the model to support multilingual legal corpora across different Indian languages to bridge language barriers in legal access; Integration with legal ontology frameworks and knowledge graphs to enable more complex tasks such as legal outcome prediction and cross-case contradiction detection; Further development of Explainable AI (XAI) and legal reasoning traces to make AI-assisted legal research defensible in formal legal proceedings

research_focus: The paper addresses the limitations of basic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines for legal information retrieval and proposes an enhanced RAG pipeline tailored to improve accuracy and relevancy when searching large volumes of legal documents such as statutes and case law.
method: The enhanced RAG pipeline integrates a multi-layered chunking strategy, enhanced metadata annotations, a hybrid search mechanism combining sparse and dense vector embeddings within a vector database, query expansion techniques, and dynamically applied metadata filters. Performance is evaluated by comparing the advanced RAG against a naive RAG setup on a benchmark dataset of 300 questions derived from Supreme Court of India judgments.
application_domain: Legal information retrieval and legal research, specifically searching through statutes, case law, and judicial precedents
results_summary: The authors constructed a benchmark dataset of 300 legal questions based on Supreme Court of India judgments and compared a naive RAG pipeline against their advanced RAG pipeline. research_focus: How retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) AI agents can transform accounting and bookkeeping workflows by leveraging vector databases and semantic understanding to overcome the limitations of traditional rule-based transaction categorization systems.
method: The paper discusses a RAG-based architecture combining vector databases for semantic matching, sophisticated document processing pipelines, cross-verification protocols, confidence scoring with human oversight, and intelligent anomaly detection applied to accounting tasks.
application_domain: Accounting and bookkeeping, including transaction categorization, financial record cross-verification, compliance monitoring, and anomaly detection.
results_summary: The paper addresses the limitations of traditional rule-based accounting systems by proposing RAG-powered AI agents that leverage vector databases for semantic transaction understanding. Citing prior studies, it reports that intelligent automation can reduce error rates by up to 82% in transaction processing and decrease reconciliation time by approximately 65%, while identifying up to 91% of accounting irregularities. In contrast, traditional systems correctly categorize only 63% of transactions without human intervention, with error rates increasing by 28% for ambiguous vendor descriptions. The paper demonstrates that implementation benefits vary across organization types, with small businesses gaining cost efficiency, accounting firms enhancing service capacity, and enterprises achieving standardization and control. Future evolution is projected toward predictive capabilities, natural language interfaces, cross-entity learning, and automated regulatory adaptation.

research_gaps: Predictive accounting capabilities; Natural language interfaces for accounting workflows; Cross-entity learning across organizations; Automated regulatory adaptation; Privacy-preserving collaborative learning

research_focus: The transformative impact of artificial intelligence (neural networks, time-series algorithms, vector databases) on cloud network capacity planning and predictive maintenance, examining the shift from reactive to proactive operational models in multi-cloud infrastructure management.
method: The paper reviews and synthesizes the deployment of hybrid AI approaches combining statistical methods with deep learning, examines empirical evidence of their effectiveness, and discusses organizational deployment strategies (cross-functional teams, incremental deployment) alongside emerging research directions.
application_domain: Cloud network capacity planning, predictive maintenance, multi-cloud resource allocation, and infrastructure reliability management
results_summary: The paper surveys how AI technologies including neural networks, time-series algorithms, and vector databases are reshaping cloud network management from reactive to proactive paradigms. research_focus: The potential integration of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems into academic library search and retrieval, including technical requirements, implementation challenges, and prospective benefits for scholarly information discovery.
method: Qualitative analysis and discussion of RAG architecture components (embedding pipelines, vector databases, middleware), their fit with academic library infrastructure, and the ethical, legal, and practical considerations for deployment.

research_gaps: Development of lightweight and scalable RAG implementations specifically designed for the unique requirements of academic libraries; Refining RAG's technical architecture to address library-specific needs; Exploring cost-effective adaptations for resource-constrained environments; Developing comprehensive frameworks to ensure ethical compliance; Addressing questions of implementation responsibility and the need for collaborative frameworks across libraries

research_focus: Proposing PDX, a new vertical data layout for vectors that stores dimensions dimension-by-dimension within blocks, to accelerate exact and approximate vector similarity search, particularly when combined with dimension-pruning algorithms such as ADSampling and BSA.
method: Design of the PDX data layout (dimension-at-a-time block storage), the PDXearch search framework that performs adaptive dimension-by-dimension scanning, and the PDX-BOND pruning algorithm that accesses the most query-relevant dimensions first without preprocessing. Evaluated on 10 vector datasets across 4 CPU architectures (Zen4, Intel Sapphire Rapids, Zen3, Graviton4) using scalar auto-vectorized code.
mentioned_systems: FAISS; Milvus; USearch; Parquet; PDXearch; PDX-BOND
indexing_methods: IVF; HNSW; ADSampling; BSA; BOND; FNN; quantization; bucketing; trees; graphs
application_domain: Vector similarity search (KNN search) as a core component for information/multimedia retrieval, data pipelines, code co-piloting, and LLM pipelines
results_summary: PDX with PDXearch achieves on average 40% faster distance computation than SIMD-optimized kernels on standard horizontal vector storage, using only scalar auto-vectorized code. ADSampling and BSA, which can lose to SIMD-optimized linear scans on the horizontal layout, regain a 2-7x speedup when applied on PDX. PDXearch achieves 5.3x faster searches than FAISS IVF_FLAT on average in high-dimensional datasets. PDX-BOND outperforms USearch, Milvus, and FAISS on exact search by 4.0x, 3.3x, and 2.5x on average, while requiring no data preprocessing and supporting exact search without recall trade-off.
limitations: PDX-BOND achieves only reasonable (not best-in-class) performance on approximate search compared to its strong exact-search performance; The PDX layout requires physically storing data in the transposed vertical format; on-the-fly gather-based transposition is never faster than PDX due to increased micro-ops and memory stalls
research_gaps: Pruning algorithms can benefit from GPU processing, which is not explored in this work; Fusing the PDX-BOND idea (query-based dimension reordering) with ADSampling (random sampling of projections at different levels) could further improve pruning power

It fills a gap in the Julia package ecosystem where no disk-backed ANN implementation with transaction support previously existed. The design builds on established disk-based ANN research (DiskANN, LM-DiskANN) while providing a simple, cross-platform installation.

research_focus: Accelerating approximate k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) search in vector databases by optimizing matrix-vector operations using a Coarse-Grained Linear Array (CGLA) architecture (IMAX3), specifically targeting the post-clustering phase of the IVF technique where matrix-vector multiplication dominates computational cost.
method: Design and implementation of a vector-distance computation kernel on the IMAX3 CGLA architecture that leverages large on-PE local memory to retain database vectors between queries, eliminating the need to reload vectors for subsequent queries. The approach jointly optimizes the computational kernel and the data-movement strategy, co-designing algorithmic choices with the hardware's memory hierarchy.
mentioned_systems: OpenSearch; Elasticsearch; Pinecone; Milvus; Faiss; ScaNN; RUMMY; FANNS; SPANN; Knowhere; IMAX3; RTX 4090; i9-10920X
indexing_methods: IVF; HNSW; PQ; IVF-PQ; IVFADC; Inverted Multi-Index
application_domain: Approximate nearest neighbor search in vector databases, with applications in recommendation systems, semantic search engines, image feature search, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for large language models.
results_summary: The paper proposes IMAX3, a CGLA-based architecture, as the first exploitation of CGLA for ANNS, targeting the post-clustering matrix-vector multiplication phase of IVF. By retaining vectors in local PE memory across queries, the method eliminates repeated vector loading and achieves up to a 54.9× speedup for repeat queries compared to the initial execution (excluding overhead). Relative to the RTX 4090, the energy-delay product (EDP) is reduced by up to 498.41× and on average 185.23×. The FPGA implementation's kernel execution time is far lower than that of a 24-core i9-10920X, demonstrating that memory-transfer efficiency is a critical bottleneck that hardware-level optimization can address.
limitations: The implementation operates at lower frequencies due to the FPGA platform rather than an ASIC; The system is deployed in an environment with multiple connected boards, adding practical complexity; The reported speedup figures exclude overhead, implying non-negligible overhead exists in practice; Energy-delay product figures are based on a 28 nm process estimate rather than the more advanced nodes used by comparison hardware
research_gaps: Research targeting the efficiency of memory transfers in vector search has received comparatively little attention relative to similarity computation acceleration; ASIC implementations at more advanced process nodes could yield even greater performance and energy improvements than the FPGA results demonstrate

research_focus: Precise multi-objective mix design of dam concrete (targeting strength, durability, and crack resistance) by proposing an intelligent generation system (DCMPS) that integrates a knowledge graph with a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework to enable interpretable and traceable mix proportioning.

results_summary: The DCMPS was validated on a test dataset and demonstrated superior overall performance compared to a larger-parameter native LLM, confirming that knowledge augmentation significantly enhances the performance of smaller models. research_focus: Accurate multivariate time series forecasting for vector database workloads, specifically addressing the challenges of capturing multiscale temporal dependencies and effectively integrating external data in highly dynamic, non-stationary workload patterns.
method: MSP-EDA combines Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) and adaptive Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) for time-frequency decomposition, constructs multiscale patches processed by dedicated encoders with temporal attention, channel correlation attention, and cross-attention with external data, and uses a trainable global token to fuse information across temporal scales.
application_domain: Vector database workload forecasting for adaptive resource scheduling, performance tuning, and system scalability; also evaluated on general domains including economics, traffic, healthcare, and cloud computing resource utilization.
results_summary: The paper proposes MSP-EDA, a forecasting framework that integrates multiscale patching with external data augmentation to model complex temporal patterns in vector database workloads. Extensive experiments on four public benchmark datasets and three real-world vector database datasets (Dvdb, Mvdb, Wvdb) show that MSP-EDA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On the vector database datasets, MSP-EDA improves MSE by 1.4% on Dvdb, 2.1% on Mvdb, and 1.9% on Wvdb compared to the second-best TimeXer model. Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of each module and the adaptability of the framework to complex forecasting scenarios involving external dependencies.
limitations: The relatively complex architecture can hinder deployment in real-time or resource-constrained environments; The integration of multiple modules and attention mechanisms reduces interpretability, making it difficult to trace and explain prediction outcomes
research_gaps: Simplifying the model through techniques such as model pruning and knowledge distillation to reduce computational complexity without sacrificing accuracy; Incorporating attention visualization, feature attribution approaches like SHAP or Integrated Gradients, and modular analysis to better understand how the model makes forecasting decisions

research_focus: Building a privacy-centric, offline chatbot using locally managed Large Language Models that handles document-based queries without internet connectivity, addressing the privacy and connectivity limitations of cloud-based chatbot solutions.
method: Integration of locally managed LLMs (Ollama, Llama.cpp) with the BGE M3 embedding model, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), vector indexing search, the Unstructured.io library for semantic document partitioning, LlamaIndex for query handling and document indexing, and Gradio for the user interface.

results_summary: The paper proposes and implements an offline AI chatbot system that processes uploaded documents, indexes their content, and generates context-aware responses using locally managed LLMs without requiring internet connectivity. research_focus: Systematic empirical evaluation of using vector databases for retrieving related occupations from the O*NET occupational database, comparing text-based similarity retrieval against curated explicit relations, and analyzing the impact of different document structures, sentence embeddings, and retrieval configurations.
method: Experimental evaluation of two open-source vector databases (Milvus and Chroma) with varying document compositions, sentence embedding models, and distance metrics, benchmarked against curated related-occupation relations in O*NET. Statistical significance tested via Kruskal-Wallis H-test; relative influence of configuration elements assessed via mutual information estimation using scikit-learn.
mentioned_systems: Milvus; Chroma; O*NET; ESCO; JobBERT; CareerBERT; all_mpnet_base_v2; gbert-base; scikit-learn
application_domain: Career planning and occupational analysis; retrieval of related occupations for job search, career transition, and RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) pipelines
results_summary: The paper evaluated two open-source vector databases (Milvus and Chroma) for related-occupation retrieval using the O*NET database, varying embeddings, distance metrics, and text composition. Results showed that all three configuration elements (distance metric, sentence embedding, text fragment selection) are statistically significant for retrieval performance, with text composition being the most influential factor. Precision is high (above 0.8) for small result cutoffs (k < 5), making the approach suitable for RAG and few-shot prompting settings. Text-based retrieval only partially overlaps with curated explicit relations but also discovers cross-cutting relations that span major occupation groupings, suggesting it complements rather than replaces curated relations. The two databases showed very small differences in overall quality, indicating that configuration choices rather than database implementation are the primary determinants of retrieval performance.
limitations: The evaluation does not consider any concrete context-specific task (e.g., career shift vs. career growth in the same domain), which could change the relative importance of different text elements; It is difficult to assess how limitations in O*NET's content coverage (sparse in some areas, redundant in others) affect retrieval metrics; No alternative occupational databases were found that could be used to mitigate the potential O*NET content limitations
research_gaps: Expert assessment of discovered relations (retrieved occupations not in the curated set) is left for future work; Future work should assess the combination of vector databases with LLMs in RAG or GraphRAG patterns, accounting for the separate contribution of the retrieval component and the LLM; Further experimentation with other occupational databases such as ESCO, which have important differences in database schemas, contents, scope, and coverage

research_focus: Addressing the fragmentation, heterogeneity, and unstructured nature of knowledge resources in earthquake emergency management by proposing a framework that integrates LLMs with knowledge representation to construct a domain-specific knowledge graph and a hybrid retrieval-augmented generation system for decision support.
method: A three-stage pipeline: (1) designing an ontology covering the full emergency management cycle (prevention, preparedness, response, recovery); (2) using structured prompts to guide LLMs in extracting entities, relationships, and attributes from unstructured documents; (3) performing knowledge fusion via HDBSCAN clustering, embedding-based similarity, and LLM validation. The resulting KG is then used in an Improved HybridRAG framework that combines symbolic retrieval from the KG with semantic similarity-based retrieval from a vector database.
application_domain: Earthquake emergency management and disaster response decision-making
results_summary: The framework was applied to a corpus of 2,682 professional documents, extracting 284,801 entities and over 80,000 unique relationship types, which were consolidated into approximately 1,000 categories and refined into a KG of over 268,000 nodes and 833,000 relationships. The Improved HybridRAG system was evaluated on a newly constructed dataset of 150 earthquake-specific questions against baselines including LLM-only, semantic vector-based retrieval, and purely symbolic retrieval. The hybrid approach significantly outperformed all baselines across accuracy, clarity, comprehensiveness, conciseness, and relevance. The results validate the advantage of combining structured symbolic knowledge retrieval with semantic vector-based retrieval for generating contextually grounded responses in earthquake emergency scenarios.
limitations: Attribute gaps in some entities limit the depth and completeness of knowledge representation; Reduced flexibility when handling nuanced or open-ended queries; System remains sensitive to the underlying quality of the knowledge graph; Entity alignment based on representation similarity may fail to distinguish subtle semantic differences between closely related entities; The graph lacks sufficient hierarchical structure, restricting deep layered querying and relationship interpretability; Embedding similarity may introduce lexically or topically related but operationally irrelevant entities, causing noise in retrieval context; Coreference resolution does not fully resolve long-range dependencies across documents, resulting in incomplete or fragmented coreference chains; Contextual metadata such as source reliability, temporal validity, and geographic scope are not explicitly modeled; Potential limitations and biases may arise from both the data sources and evaluation methods
research_gaps: Improving attribute completeness in the knowledge graph; Refining entity alignment techniques to capture complex semantic nuances; Exploring multimodal data integration (spatial layers, maps, sensor signals) to extend the KG's utility; Developing domain-specific embedding models fine-tuned on earthquake-related corpora for more precise entity alignment; Integrating intelligent agent-based mechanisms to dynamically adjust query strategies based on intent, context, and real-time constraints; Exploring document-level or graph-based coreference models to handle long-range dependencies; Incorporating intelligent chunking or controlled overlap strategies to maintain reference continuity while minimizing redundancy; Incorporating metadata-aware reasoning mechanisms and expanding the ontology to include contextual dimensions (source reliability, temporal validity, geographic scope); Fine-tuning generation models for improved handling of earthquake-specific terminology and operational logic

research_focus: Enhancing large language models for STEMM research and education by leveraging transcribed audio podcast content and integrating a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline with a vector database for real-time access to scientific literature.
method: Transcribed over 3700 hours of publicly available STEMM audio podcasts (yielding 42+ million text tokens) and used this data to pre-train/fine-tune LLMs (Gemma, LLaMA). A RAG framework was implemented on top of a vector database constructed from journal articles to provide real-time access to emerging scientific literature. The resulting model, PodGPT, was evaluated on medical QA benchmarks (MedQA, PubMedQA, MedMCQA), MMLU STEMM categories, and multilingual zero-shot tasks.
application_domain: STEMM research and education, including medical patient-physician dialogue, multilingual scientific question answering, and conversational AI
results_summary: PodGPT was trained on transcribed STEMM podcast audio and evaluated against baseline models (Gemma, LLaMA) on multiple benchmarks. The model demonstrated an average improvement of 1.82 percentage points over standard open-source benchmarks and 2.43 percentage points when augmented with the RAG pipeline. Zero-shot multilingual transfer ability improved by an average of 1.18 percentage points. Performance gains were more pronounced with lightweight models (Gemma 2B/7B) compared to larger models (LLaMA 3.3 70B), highlighting a scalability consideration. Lower perplexity scores on a conversational dataset confirmed improved coherence in medical dialogue generation.
limitations: Limited to openly available STEMM audio podcast content based on the CC BY license; Model was trained exclusively on English podcasts; Vast collections of available but unharnessed data (e.g., textbooks, video tutorials) could not be leveraged due to licensing restrictions
research_gaps: Acquiring diverse and legally accessible podcast data in multiple languages; Incorporating more peer-reviewed journal content to enrich training and enhance multilingual model performance; Conducting a comprehensive ethical evaluation to ensure the model adheres to high scientific standards across settings; Performing a detailed error analysis to provide a more balanced assessment of model performance

research_focus: Integration of Large Language Models and secure Gen-AI technologies (RAG with vector embeddings and ANN search) to improve inventory management, component selection, and recommendation workflows in engineering design and manufacturing.
method: A Python 3.11-based API system that converts user queries into 384-dimensional vector embeddings using the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 transformer model, performs ANN search in a vector database (similarity threshold 0.7, top-5 results), and uses an LLM to generate context-aware recommendations. Data privacy is preserved through selective obfuscation using the ROT13 algorithm. The embedding model was optionally fine-tuned with domain-specific part lists and sample queries.
application_domain: Manufacturing and engineering design, specifically inventory management and component/part selection in a control panel manufacturing facility.
results_summary: The research focus was addressed by implementing and deploying an LLM-based RAG system in a real-world control panel manufacturing facility, using vector embeddings and ANN search for similarity-based retrieval of inventory items. Real-world testing with an industry sponsor demonstrated strong performance: 88.4% Answer Relevance, 92.1% Faithfulness, 80.2% Context Recall, and 83.1% Context Precision. These results indicate the system can deliver accurate and relevant responses while retrieving meaningful context and minimizing irrelevant information. The approach is presented as a practical, privacy-aware solution that bridges the gap between traditional keyword-based inventory tools and modern AI capabilities for more intelligent design and production workflows.
research_gaps: Extensibility of the solution to other domains requiring intelligent inventory or product search beyond the manufacturing context in which it was validated

research_focus: Efficient and accurate classification of geographic text in Earth observation data, addressing challenges of data sparsity, class imbalance, semantic ambiguity, and domain-specific terminology that hinder traditional classification approaches.
method: A two-stage LLM framework (HierLabelNet) that combines LLM-based data augmentation to mitigate data scarcity and class imbalance, a semantic vector database to filter the label space prior to inference, few-shot prompt learning for domain-specific language understanding, and an output alignment mechanism to improve classification stability.
application_domain: Geographic text classification for Earth observation data, including GIS, disaster response, and smart city information management
results_summary: The paper proposes HierLabelNet, a two-stage LLM framework that integrates data augmentation, semantic vector-based label filtering, few-shot prompting, and output alignment for geographic text classification. Under extremely low-shot conditions (Q=1), the framework yielded substantial improvements, e.g., macro-F1 increased by 28.85% for Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and by 6.14% for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Cross-model evaluations showed that generative LLMs such as the LLaMA3.1 series exhibited greater responsiveness, with consistent gains from Q=1 to Q=8. However, performance improvements plateau as Q increases, with marginal gains dropping below 2%, indicating computational bottlenecks in current LLM architectures for assimilating large volumes of semantic examples. Overall, the framework delivers higher efficiency and reduced token consumption in the low-Q regime, favorable for real-world deployment.
limitations: The effectiveness of the framework is inherently influenced by the capabilities of the underlying embedding models and LLMs; As the number of contextual examples (Q) increases, performance improvements plateau with marginal gains diminishing to below 2%, indicating computational bottlenecks in current LLM architectures for assimilating large volumes of semantic examples
research_gaps: Constructing higher-quality and larger-scale domain-specific datasets to enable more effective fine-tuning of embedding models and LLMs for EO domain knowledge; Extending the applicability of the framework to multimodal EO data classification scenarios, integrating heterogeneous sources such as images, text, and spatiotemporal data

research_focus: Systematization and comparative analysis of sharding strategies for distributed vector databases, with the goal of proposing a multi-criteria framework for selecting optimal scaling strategies under heterogeneous AI workloads.
method: Review and synthesis of advances in distributed vector database architectures and partitioning techniques from scientific publications and technical reports, followed by a comparative analysis based on latency, throughput, recall/precision, and load balancing criteria, culminating in a proposed multi-criteria decision-making framework.
application_domain: Semantic search and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems in generative AI
results_summary: The paper conducted a comparative analysis of sharding strategies—including data partitioning, query parallelism, and hybrid configurations—for distributed vector databases. It found that hybrid strategies combining content-aware partitioning with replica-parallel query processing demonstrate the greatest versatility and efficiency under heterogeneous workloads. Content-oriented partitioning with smart request routing showed higher QPS values compared to simple hash-based sharding, as it eliminates unnecessary scanning of irrelevant segments. The authors proposed a multi-criteria framework decision model that considers data volume, latency and throughput requirements, data characteristics, and economic costs to guide strategy selection. The study concluded that traditional static distribution schemes lose effectiveness as vector volumes grow, necessitating flexible distributed architectures.
research_gaps: Development of self-adaptive sharding mechanisms based on machine learning methods, capable of reconfiguring the distribution of shards and replicas in real time in response to changes in data patterns and the nature of user queries

research_focus: Accelerating streaming subgraph matching by replacing kd-tree-based indexing with a vector database that performs k-nearest neighbor search on high-dimensional graph embeddings, enabling effective caching and reuse of query results under high query arrival rates.
method: The paper adopts a framework that generates subgraph embeddings via message passing neural networks (MPNN), then performs kNN search on these high-dimensional vectors using a vector database with inverted file (IVF) and product quantization (PQ) indexing techniques to accelerate the process and support cache-based query reuse.
indexing_methods: IVF (Inverted File); PQ (Product Quantization); kd-tree; IndexIVFPQ
application_domain: Streaming subgraph matching in graph databases, with broader applications in social network analysis, bioinformatics, recommendation systems, fraud detection, and network anomaly detection
results_summary: The paper addresses streaming subgraph matching by leveraging a vector database with IVF and PQ indexing for kNN search on MPNN-generated graph embeddings, replacing the less efficient kd-tree baseline. Experimental evaluations on 16 diverse real-world datasets demonstrate an average 87.7% reduction in processing time compared to the state-of-the-art kd-tree-based method. Cache hit rates range from 70% to 90% across varying batch sizes, and a cache size of 20,000 was identified as optimal for balancing accuracy and computational efficiency. Search times scale linearly from 40 ms to 176 ms as batch sizes increase from 5,000 to 20,000, confirming the framework's robustness and scalability.
research_gaps: Refining methods for batched streaming subgraph matching; Addressing hardware challenges; Addressing algorithmic challenges; Enhancing efficiency and scalability of batched streaming subgraph matching tasks

research_focus: The technological evolution of search engines from early keyword-matching systems to AI-powered search, covering NLP, transformer models, LLMs, RAG, and vector databases, along with applications and associated challenges.
method: A structured literature review tracing the historical development of information retrieval, from Boolean and Vector Space Models through LSI, PageRank, BERT, and modern LLM-based and RAG-based retrieval, while discussing architectural principles, applications, and open challenges.
application_domain: E-commerce, healthcare, and academic research
results_summary: The paper surveys the full trajectory of search engine technology, from early keyword-matching systems (Archie, AltaVista) through statistical and neural methods (PageRank, BERT) to current AI-enabled systems leveraging LLMs, RAG, and vector databases. It identifies that modern search engines go beyond word matching to assess user intent, provide personalized results, and generate answers within a RAG framework. The review highlights that while these systems improve accuracy and relevance, they introduce significant challenges including algorithmic bias, misinformation, SEO poisoning, and privacy concerns. The paper concludes by outlining future directions in conversational AI, multimodal retrieval, and generative retrieval systems.
limitations: Algorithmic bias in AI-driven search engines; Misinformation propagation; SEO poisoning and manipulation of rankings; Privacy concerns associated with AI-enabled search
research_gaps: Conversational AI for search; Multimodal retrieval; Generative retrieval systems

research_focus: The paper addresses the challenge of analyzing large volumes of customer feedback (online reviews) by proposing a system that uses LLMs integrated with advanced RAG techniques (Hierarchical Chunk Retrieval, RAG Fusion) and the DSPy framework to answer natural language queries over customer reviews.
method: A synthetic dataset of food delivery reviews was created and stored in a vector database. The system employs Hierarchical Chunk Retrieval and RAG Fusion for retrieval, refined by the DSPy framework for iterative query rewriting and multi-hop reasoning. Three LLMs (LLaMA-3-8B-InstructLite, GPT-3.5-Turbo, Gemini-1.5-Pro) were evaluated against BM25 and a fine-tuned BERT baseline using BERT Score, ROUGE, and RAGAS metrics.
mentioned_systems: LangChain; DSPy; LLaMA-3-8B-InstructLite; GPT-3.5-Turbo; Gemini-1.5-Pro; RAGAS; BM25; BERT
indexing_methods: Hierarchical Chunk Retrieval; RAG Fusion; Reciprocal Rank Fusion; BM25; semantic similarity via embeddings
application_domain: Customer feedback analysis and online review summarization
results_summary: The proposed LLM-based pipeline outperforms non-LLM baselines (BM25 and fine-tuned BERT) by an average of 15% in semantic and factual accuracy. Component-level analysis shows that enhanced retrieval strategies (Hierarchical Chunk Retrieval and RAG Fusion) yield aggregate improvements of 4.9% in semantic relevance, 12.1% in lexical coverage, and 9.9% in factual consistency over traditional RAG. Further integration of DSPy provides an additional 10.8% boost in linguistic fluency and a 9.0% gain in factual alignment. Among the evaluated models, Gemini-1.5-Pro combined with RAG Fusion and DSPy produced the most fluent and factually accurate responses, demonstrating the effectiveness of combining hybrid retrieval with LLM-driven reasoning.
limitations: Traditional RAG frequently recovers semantically related fragments while omitting more complex, interrelated meanings, with up to 90% of potentially helpful content potentially missed; BM25 lacks semantic understanding and fails to capture context beyond word matching, limiting its suitability for feedback-driven natural language response generation; The fine-tuned BERT model is highly sensitive to input length and phrasing, can only process a limited window of text, and is unable to reason across multiple reviews or adapt to alternate phrasings; Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-Lite shows improvable performance, particularly in Faithfulness and Factual Correctness

research_focus: Design and implementation of a modular, privacy-preserving conversational AI chatbot framework that integrates Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with a hybrid recommender engine, operating entirely on local infrastructure using local LLMs to address hallucination, limited context retention, and poor personalization.
method: The system uses LangChain to orchestrate a RAG pipeline, FAISS for vector indexing and semantic similarity search, the Ollama runtime to host local LLMs (Mistral), NLP pipelines (tokenization, lemmatization, stop-word removal) for text preprocessing, and a hybrid recommender combining TF-IDF keyword extraction with dense vector ranking. Evaluation was conducted on mid-range hardware (Intel i7, 16 GB RAM, 6 GB VRAM GPU) with manual relevance assessment and an ablation study.
mentioned_systems: FAISS; LangChain; Ollama; Mistral; Flask; spaCy; NLTK; Docker; Locust; JMeter; GPT-4; Cohere
indexing_methods: FAISS vector indexing; TF-IDF; dense vector ranking; Recursive Character Text Splitter (chunking)
application_domain: Conversational AI / document-based question answering / knowledge management
results_summary: The modular framework was implemented and evaluated on mid-range hardware, achieving retrieval times under 0.5 seconds for datasets of up to 5,000 chunks and an average end-to-end response time of approximately 1.2 seconds. The hybrid recommender engine achieved over 85% relevance in manual evaluation, and an ablation study confirmed that disabling retrieval significantly increased hallucinated outputs while removing the recommender lowered user engagement. The system demonstrated effective local, privacy-preserving operation without cloud dependency. However, limitations were observed in multilingual handling, long-form technical queries, and cases where no corresponding document existed for a query.
limitations: Hallucination occurs when user queries lack corresponding documents in the knowledge base; TF-IDF-based recommendations occasionally produce semantically irrelevant suggestions for heterogeneous datasets; Lacks robust multilingual handling; Struggles with long-form or highly technical queries; Tested primarily in a single-user, research-focused setting rather than multi-user production environments; No formal benchmarking against cloud-based LLM systems (e.g., GPT-4, Cohere) has been conducted
research_gaps: Multi-document handling and real-time interaction improvements; Deeper personalization and adaptive recommendations (e.g., reinforcement learning); Benchmarking against commercial RAG systems and cloud-based LLMs (GPT-4, Cohere) to quantify trade-offs in latency, cost, and output quality; Integration of standardized generation metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore); Development of threat models and privacy-preserving mechanisms (differential privacy, embedding encryption); Incorporation of explainability frameworks (SHAP, LIME); Large-scale user studies using System Usability Scale and Likert-scale ratings; Multimodal extensions including OCR-based document parsing and voice-based interaction; Multi-user concurrency testing using load-testing tools (Locust, JMeter); Domain-specific fine-tuning, document enrichment, and multilingual embedding support

research_focus: Development of the Alumni Intelligence System, a scalable and intelligent solution that integrates LLaMA 3 with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and a vector database to preserve and enable intelligent access to alumni project data within an academic institution.
method: The system uses the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model to create vector embeddings from structured alumni project data, stores them in a vector database, performs similarity search upon receiving a query to retrieve relevant contexts, and then uses LLaMA 3 to generate accurate and context-aware responses. The system was built using Python, Pandas, GROQ, and Next.js, and was trained on a dataset of approximately 155 final-year student projects.
mentioned_systems: LLaMA 3; Llama 2; Llama-3 8B; Llama-2 7B; all-MiniLM-L6-v2; LangChain; GROQ; Next.js; Python; Pandas; ChatGPT; DALL•E; Midjourney; Falcon; GPT-3; PaLM; GPT-4; Llama Guard 3; Llama 3.1; BERT-base
application_domain: Alumni project data management and academic knowledge retention in educational institutions
results_summary: The paper developed and evaluated the Alumni Intelligence System by integrating LLaMA 3 with RAG and a vector database for alumni project data retrieval and generation. Performance evaluation showed strong results: Cosine Similarity of 0.78, Precision@5 of 0.79, Hit Rate@5 of 0.90, MAP of 0.73, ROUGE-L of 0.74, and BLEU score of 0.64. The Average Euclidean Distance of 0.19 confirmed semantic closeness of retrieved vectors. The system demonstrated its ability to generate context-aware responses to alumni-related queries based on 155 indexed project records. Overall, the findings support the viability of combining vector-based retrieval with large language models for academic knowledge management.
limitations: Room for improvement in response fluency, as indicated by the BLEU score of 0.64; Minor opportunities for improvement in stylistic diversity and language variability; Limited dataset of only 155 usable records due to limited and outdated historical records; Challenges of hallucinations and prompt sensitivity inherent to LLMs
research_gaps: Improving response fluency and stylistic diversity in generated text; Scaling the system beyond the limited 155-record dataset to handle larger alumni data collections

research_focus: Systematization and comparative analysis of fault-tolerant replication approaches in vector search systems, examining trade-offs between data consistency, service availability, and response time in the context of RAG architectures and generative AI workloads.
method: Systematic and comparative analysis of academic publications and technical documentation of leading industry solutions, categorizing replication models and evaluating their characteristics along multiple criteria (consistency, latency, throughput, fault tolerance, implementation complexity).
mentioned_systems: Activeloop Deep Lake; Amazon S3; Google Cloud Storage
application_domain: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures, generative AI systems, semantic search over heterogeneous unstructured data (text, images, audio), online recommendations, financial calculations, medical records
results_summary: The paper identified and characterized three main classes of replication approaches in vector search systems: leader-follower (primary-backup), consensus-based protocols (e.g., Raft, Paxos), and shared-storage architectures. A comparative analysis showed that no single model simultaneously provides ideal consistency, availability, latency, and ease of deployment, confirming the CAP-theorem-driven trade-offs. The study demonstrated that the choice of replication scheme is determined by the combination of throughput, latency, fault-tolerance requirements, and financial/operational constraints. The authors concluded that hybrid solutions—using consensus protocols for metadata management combined with leader-follower replication for vector index segments—offer the optimal balance between reliability and cost. The findings provide methodological guidance for system architects designing scalable, fault-tolerant AI applications.

research_focus: Development and evaluation of NOVA, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) educational virtual assistant for teaching Parallel Computing in Spanish, addressing the lack of linguistically appropriate AI-driven learning tools for Spanish-speaking students in technical CS courses.
method: A modular RAG architecture combining a Qdrant vector database for semantic retrieval of course-specific materials with the GPT-4o mini LLM for context-aware response generation, deployed via a FastAPI backend, Next.js frontend, and n8n automation server. The system was evaluated using a test suite of 100 academic tasks (55 Q&A prompts, 25 practical guides, 20 quizzes) measuring response time, quality rating, and retrieval coverage.
mentioned_systems: Qdrant; FastAPI; Next.js; n8n; GPT-4o mini; NotebookLM; KG-RAG; OpenMP; MPI; CUDA; PyCUDA
application_domain: Technical education (Parallel Computing course), specifically semantic retrieval of course materials for generating pedagogically aligned Q&A, quizzes, and practical guides in Spanish
results_summary: NOVA was developed as a five-component modular RAG system and deployed at Universidad Politécnica Salesiana for the Parallel Computing course. Evaluation across 100 test cases showed a 92% excellence rating, a 21-second average response time, and 72% retrieval coverage of relevant fragments. The authors attribute the high accuracy to the combination of a curated academic corpus, targeted prompt engineering, and temperature tuning (0.2–0.35) to balance corpus grounding with the LLM's internal knowledge. The 72% coverage metric was identified as partly reflecting gaps in the curated corpus, mitigated by allowing the model to supplement with internal knowledge. The results confirm that RAG architectures with domain-aligned materials can produce reliable, pedagogically coherent content in a specialized, non-English educational setting.
limitations: Evaluation conducted on a limited sample of 100 test cases designed by the development team without direct end-user input during validation; Metrics such as coverage and relevance rely on subjective interpretation of retrieval adequacy and may be influenced by manual annotation of metadata and corpus selection; Absence of formal usability testing or inter-rater reliability analysis limits generalizability of findings; Corpus was specific to one institution and course, so potential overfitting to its content cannot be ruled out; Reliance on commercial LLMs and dedicated vector databases entails costs that may be challenging for some institutions; Cultural and linguistic biases can still arise due to regional variations in Spanish or the way instructional materials are curated

research_focus: Presenting a domain-adapted Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework for real-time financial market analysis that combines vector databases with domain-specific language models to address the limitations of static NLP models in handling dynamic, unstructured financial data.
method: A modular RAG architecture featuring domain-specific preprocessing, vector storage using ChromaDB, and fine-tuned generative models (BART), evaluated quantitatively via BLEU, ROUGE, FEVER, and FactCC metrics, and qualitatively through human evaluation by experienced financial analysts.
application_domain: Real-time financial market analysis, including earnings calls, SEC filings, social media, global news, and investment decision support
results_summary: The paper designed and evaluated a domain-adapted RAG framework for real-time financial analysis, combining ChromaDB for vector storage with a fine-tuned BART generative model. Quantitative evaluation showed superior accuracy and factuality compared to traditional NLP models, with high BLEU and ROUGE scores and strong performance on FEVER and FactCC metrics, significantly reducing hallucinations. The system also achieved low latency and high throughput suitable for real-time financial environments. Human evaluation by financial analysts yielded high scores: contextual correctness averaged 4.3/5, business value 4.1/5, and interpretability 4.6/5, with analysts particularly valuing the transparent source attribution and confidence scoring mechanisms.
limitations: Data source quality and bias: inherent biases in news reporting or social media discussions can be perpetuated and amplified by the system if not carefully monitored; Handling conflicting information: the system faces challenges in resolving direct contradictions between authoritative sources and lacks a sophisticated mechanism for this
research_gaps: Enhanced real-time data ingestion to incorporate ephemeral sources such as high-frequency trading signals and live audio feeds from earnings calls; Advanced ambiguity handling for nuanced or ambiguous financial language, potentially using reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF); Multimodal integration of financial charts, news videos, and satellite imagery for richer contextual analysis; Personalization of RAG systems to adapt to individual analyst preferences, risk profiles, and specific investment strategies

research_focus: Whether an AI-driven tool based on professors' notes and course outlines can improve engineering students' learning outcomes by providing immediate, relevant, syllabus-aligned answers, demonstrated through the implementation of Prof-Notes AI for a mechanical engineering fluid dynamics course.
method: Full-stack application with a React/JavaScript frontend and a Python backend integrating GPT models, Llama, and Pinecone vector databases, deployed on Google App Engine with Firebase for real-time data flow and caching. Evaluation was conducted through two rounds of in-person user testing (8 and 10 participants) using a matrix-based testing framework assessing accuracy, response time, clarity, and usefulness of retrieved resources, with five-point scale ratings converted to percentage-based metrics.
mentioned_systems: Pinecone; GPT; Llama; ChatGPT; CoPilot; Google App Engine; Firebase
application_domain: Engineering education, specifically a third-year undergraduate mechanical engineering fluid dynamics course, providing course-specific Q&A, syllabus information, and technical concept explanations to students.
results_summary: The paper presents the design, implementation, and user evaluation of Prof-Notes AI, a full-stack application that categorizes student queries as technical or syllabus-related and retrieves relevant content (equations, illustrations, videos) from professor notes. Two rounds of user testing with 18 participants across diverse academic levels showed that linking answers directly to professor notes improved response relevance, and many students found the tool reliable. The system was tested across multiple devices and browsers, confirming adaptability. However, users identified challenges with complex, multi-step queries and the inability to interpret trends in graphical data. Overall, the results support the viability of AI-driven, syllabus-aligned Q&A tools for engineering education, though further refinement in answer depth and response ranking is needed.
limitations: The system cannot yet analyze or interpret complex trends from supporting visual data such as graphs; Responses to complex, multi-step questions need improvement; Limited student adoption due to lack of awareness about the platform's syllabus alignment and structured learning approach; Some students noted challenges with complex queries and continued reliance on other resources

research_focus: Evaluation of HomeDOCtor, a nationally localized AI chatbot for personalized primary care guidance in Slovenia, assessing its diagnostic accuracy, contextual relevance, and practical viability compared to general-purpose LLMs in both international and national clinical contexts.
method: The system combines retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with a Redis-based vector database of curated national medical guidelines. Evaluation used 100 international clinical vignettes from the Avey AI Benchmark Suite and 150 internal medicine exam questions from the University of Ljubljana, with one-shot prompting, pairwise z-tests with Bonferroni correction, and a six-month nationwide deployment with user feedback collection.
mentioned_systems: HomeDOCtor; ChatGPT-4o; ChatGPT o3 mini high; Gemini 2.5; Gemma 3; Ollama; Redis; Avey AI Benchmark Suite
application_domain: Primary care triage, internal medicine diagnosis, and self-care guidance in the Slovenian healthcare system
results_summary: HomeDOCtor achieved 99/100 correct diagnoses on the Avey AI international vignette suite, matching or exceeding state-of-the-art commercial models. On nationally contextualized medical exam questions, HomeDOCtor 4o significantly outperformed ChatGPT-4o (90.7% vs. 80.7%, p = 0.0135), demonstrating the value of localized RAG with curated national guidelines. During its six-month nationwide deployment, the system received overwhelmingly positive user feedback with average response times under three seconds. The findings confirm that domain-specific, nationally adapted LLM architectures can outperform general-purpose models in country-specific clinical applications while remaining GDPR-compliant.
limitations: Evaluation focused primarily on internal medicine, limiting generalizability to pediatrics, elderly care, and mental health; Usability testing was limited to informal expert feedback rather than a formal usability study; Due to GDPR constraints, personalization features and long-term interaction histories are currently unavailable; The system is not yet integrated with patient electronic health records (EHRs) or biometric sensors; Absence of a formal error analysis; only informal internal reviews of incorrect responses were conducted; Differences between some model versions (e.g., HomeDOCtor o3 mini high vs. ChatGPT o3 mini high) did not reach statistical significance, possibly due to sample-size limitations

research_focus: The paper addresses the limitation of existing AI memory models in maintaining long-term memory, preserving contextual meaning, and accurately retrieving specific information fragments from large corpora. It presents StudSar, a neural associative memory system that emulates human-like mechanisms for forming, storing, and retrieving memories in AI.
method: StudSar uses a five-stage pipeline: text segmentation into semantically rich blocks, embedding generation using the 'all-MiniLM-L6-v2' model from Sentence Transformers (384-dimensional vectors), associative marker creation, integration into a custom PyTorch neural network, and query-driven similarity-based retrieval. The system incorporates metadata integration (emotional tags, reputation scores, usage frequency), dynamic memory updates, and a tensor-based memory structure for persistence.
mentioned_systems: StudSar; Sentence Transformers; PyTorch; Hugging Face Transformers; Word2Vec; BERT; GPT-3; Sentence-BERT; Neural Turing Machines; Memory Networks; DistilBERT; SpaCy
indexing_methods: cosine similarity-based retrieval; embedding-based associative retrieval
application_domain: NLP and text processing, with applications in conversational agents, personalized learning platforms, knowledge management, and educational tools
results_summary: The paper presents StudSar's architecture and validates it through a series of experiments on text segmentation, associative marker generation, context-aware retrieval, and memory persistence. Routine queries achieved cosine similarity scores of 0.665–0.798, while challenging low-context tasks scored 0.393–0.579. Dynamic update capability was confirmed by adding a new segment and retrieving it with a similarity score of 0.7981, and memory persistence was validated by saving and reloading the network state with a score of 0.7725. Stress testing with a 2-million-token corpus demonstrated stable performance with an average latency of 0.32 seconds and consistent similarity scores.
limitations: Current segmentation approach relies on word-level fallbacks in the absence of SpaCy, which may impact embedding quality for complex texts; Preliminary integration of metadata (emotional tags, reputation scores) requires further validation across diverse datasets to ensure robustness; Lack of GPU support limits scalability for large-scale AI memory tasks

research_focus: Designing and evaluating a context-aware retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system tailored for the urology domain to reduce hallucinations and improve contextual relevance and accuracy of AI-generated medical responses.
method: A context-aware RAG system was developed integrating PubMedBERT embeddings for encoding and retrieving urological literature stored in a Pinecone vector database, named entity recognition for domain-specific query filtering, dynamic memory for contextual flow, and LLaMA3-8B via LangChain for response generation. Evaluation used a custom dataset of 150 urology-related queries with LLM-based scoring via Deepseek-R1, and a subset of 50 responses was reviewed by board-certified urologists.
application_domain: Urology / clinical decision support in medical AI
results_summary: The proposed RAG-enhanced LLaMA3-8B system was benchmarked against four baseline LLaMA models (LLaMA 3 8B, LLaMA 3.1 1B, LLaMA 3.2 3B, LLaMA 3.3 70B) across 150 domain-specific urological queries. Integration of memory modules and named entity filtering further improved precision and reliability. A subset of 50 responses reviewed by board-certified urologists confirmed clinical accuracy and guideline adherence. A stress test with a fictitious disease query demonstrated the system's ability to avoid generating hallucinated medical information.
limitations: Querying large external databases can introduce delays in response time; Accuracy of responses relies on the quality and relevance of the retrieved documents; Building and maintaining the retriever and database infrastructure requires careful design and optimization; Inference latency needs to be reduced for practical clinical use; Automated validation without manual oversight is not yet achieved
research_gaps: Reducing inference latency for real-time clinical use; Improving automated validation without manual oversight; Developing dynamic periodical collection-storage algorithms to maintain data recency; Employing or implementing more effective similarity search algorithms

research_focus: Accelerating the fine search stage of IVF-based Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search (ANNS) at billion scale, where compute-intensive GEMV operations become a bottleneck under large query volumes, particularly in RAG systems.
method: CABANA, a cluster-aware query batching mechanism that aggregates queries targeting the same clusters and reformulates fine-search GEMV operations into high-throughput GEMM operations, leveraging Intel AMX's tile-based architecture to improve compute intensity and memory access regularity.
application_domain: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems requiring billion-scale vector search
results_summary: The paper addresses the fine-search bottleneck in IVF-based ANNS by proposing CABANA, which batches queries sharing the same clusters to convert GEMV into GEMM on Intel AMX. Evaluations on billion-scale datasets (SIFT1B, DEEP1B) show CABANA achieves up to 32.6× higher query throughput than AVX512-FP32 and 18.2× over AVX512-BF16 while maintaining high recall rates. The coordination overhead from cluster-aware batching remains below 6% of total latency across all configurations. research_focus: The current state of computer vision technologies applied to fashion recommendation systems, with a focus on personalized style analysis from single photographs, covering technical capabilities, commercial implementations, system architecture, scalability, and ethical frameworks.
method: A comprehensive literature review synthesizing recent research findings, industry case studies, and emerging technological developments across technical, commercial, and ethical dimensions of computer vision-based fashion recommendation.
application_domain: Fashion e-commerce and personalized style recommendation from single photographs, including visual search, virtual try-on, and automated personal shopping assistants.
results_summary: The paper surveys the state of computer vision in fashion recommendation, highlighting that Vision Transformers achieve over 95% accuracy on Fashion-MNIST and that major commercial deployments like Amazon's Shop the Look process billions of product queries. It identifies key technical architectures including multi-modal integration, vector database optimization, and hybrid processing strategies as central to system design. The review documents significant algorithmic bias, citing 34.7% error rates for dark-skinned females versus 0.8% for light-skinned males in related computer vision tasks. It concludes that while technical viability and business value are demonstrated, critical challenges in bias mitigation, privacy protection, cultural inclusivity, and technical scalability remain unresolved. Future directions point toward enhanced personalization, privacy-preserving technologies, and sustainable AI integration.
limitations: Algorithmic bias with systematic underperformance for diverse demographic populations; Privacy concerns arising from extraction of personal information from clothed photographs; Dataset diversity challenges with geographic, cultural, and demographic imbalances limiting generalization; Technical scalability challenges in deploying large-scale AI systems; The paper is confined to a literature review and does not present new empirical data; The analysis offers only a temporal snapshot of the field; Does not encompass the proprietary complexities of real-world system deployment; Does not fully address cultural biases present in common training datasets

research_focus: Automating the generation of Bloom's Taxonomy-based assessment questions that align with Course Outcomes (COs) within Outcome-Based Education (OBE) frameworks, using a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system backed by a vector database to ensure syllabus-specific, cognitively appropriate question generation.

application_domain: Educational assessment and question generation within Outcome-Based Education (OBE) frameworks
results_summary: The proposed RAG-based system was implemented and tested on a Blockchain Technology subject, generating Bloom's Taxonomy-aligned questions for specified Course Outcomes. The system demonstrated a significant reduction in manual effort and time required for question preparation compared to traditional methods. The results validate the system's effectiveness in producing high-quality, syllabus-specific questions and its adaptability to diverse domains and cognitive requirements.
research_gaps: Scaling the system across multiple subjects and educational institutions for consistent and objective question generation

research_focus: Intelligent question answering for civil aviation airworthiness certification regulations using a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) approach, addressing challenges of knowledge updating, cross-disciplinary complexity, and hierarchical structure of regulatory texts.
method: A RAG pipeline comprising a data processing stage (document conversion, information extraction, document parsing), a retrieval-based reasoning stage with a two-stage 'semantic retrieval–cross-encoder re-ranking' mechanism, and prompt optimization for generation. A 4688-entry QA dataset was constructed using an LLM-based three-stage 'generation–enhancement–correction' framework.
application_domain: Civil aviation airworthiness certification regulation question answering (NLP/information retrieval applied to aviation regulatory compliance)
results_summary: The paper constructed a 4688-entry airworthiness regulation QA dataset and designed a RAG pipeline with semantic-aware chunking, hybrid retrieval, and cross-encoder re-ranking. Experiments demonstrated significant improvements over baselines in both answer accuracy and clause retrieval hit rates across multiple-choice, true/false, and fill-in-the-blank tasks. The system can leverage the latest regulatory specifications without retraining the underlying large language model. Even pre-trained models without domain-specific fine-tuning, combined with simple retrieval, achieved a reasonable level of accuracy, highlighting the transferability of LLMs. The findings confirm that deeply integrating domain structural information with retrieval-augmented strategies is critical for improving reliability in highly regulated text scenarios.
limitations: The QA dataset does not include case corpora from real-world aircraft certification scenarios or complex cross-referencing contexts within regulatory provisions due to data collection challenges and confidentiality constraints; Model performance on fill-in-the-blank tasks is noticeably lower than on multiple-choice and true/false tasks; The model struggles with contextual constraints and highly specialized terminology, indicating insufficient fine-grained modeling of domain-specific terminology and factual consistency judgment under complex contexts
research_gaps: Incorporating non-confidential real-world certification scenario corpora and expert Q&A records to construct a more diverse dataset covering a broader range of scenarios; Integrating complex multimodal information such as diagrams commonly present in actual certification tasks, and exploring multimodal fusion retrieval and real-time update mechanisms; Incorporating constrained generation in terminology modeling and contextual condition parsing to enhance model robustness in specialized domains

research_focus: Assessing the environmental (GHG emissions) and nutritional impact of processed food products where proprietary recipe information is unavailable, by using LLMs to approximate ingredient compositions and storing the results in a vector database for real-time consumer recommendations.
method: Using LLaMA3 to infer approximate ingredient compositions from product descriptions, integrating these with the USDA Global Branded Food Products Database and emissions databases, computing NutriScore nutritional ratings, embedding the combined data into a high-dimensional vector space using sentence-transformer models, and storing it in a vector database to enable fast similarity search and filtering.
mentioned_systems: LLaMA3; sentence-transformer models; USDA Global Branded Food Products Database; NutriScore
application_domain: Food sustainability, environmental impact assessment, and consumer nutrition decision-making
results_summary: The paper presents an AI-driven framework that uses LLaMA3 to approximate ingredient compositions of food products, integrates these with emissions databases and NutriScore, and stores the combined data in a vector database for real-time similarity search. Due to the absence of a comprehensive benchmark dataset jointly covering GHG emissions and nutritional metrics, evaluation was conducted through qualitative validation grounded in domain knowledge. The model demonstrated relative consistency by correctly identifying that meat-based products (e.g., pepperoni pizza) carry higher emission scores than plant-based alternatives. The framework enables consumers to scan a product and receive instant recommendations for nutritionally superior and lower-impact alternatives without relying on proprietary manufacturing data. The system is designed for scalable deployment across diverse food markets and geographies.
limitations: Emission assessment is constrained to greenhouse gas outputs and does not incorporate water usage, land exploitation, or biodiversity effects; The framework operates independently of economic considerations such as price, which is a major factor in consumer behavior; No quantitative benchmark was feasible due to the lack of a comprehensive dataset jointly including GHG emissions and nutritional metrics for processed foods; Evaluation was limited to qualitative validation based on domain knowledge rather than rigorous quantitative testing
research_gaps: Incorporate broader environmental indicators such as water usage, land exploitation, and biodiversity effects; Integrate cost-based filtering into the vector database alongside nutritional and emission metrics; Integrate supply chain transparency mechanisms such as blockchain; Explore region-specific optimizations for the platform; Align the platform with emerging global standards in sustainable consumption and digital food labeling
