research_focus: Autonomous reconstruction of antenna geometries from unstructured scientific literature (PDFs) using a Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MRAG) framework that integrates vision-language models, vector databases, OCR, and computer vision.
method: A pipeline that extracts figures and contextual text from PDFs using PyMuPDF, generates unified multimodal embeddings with BLIP2 or LLaVA, stores them in a Chroma or FAISS vector database for semantic retrieval, uses a RAG-based reasoning loop with LangChain/LangGraph for orchestration, applies Tesseract/EasyOCR for dimension label extraction, uses Stable Diffusion Inpainting to remove annotations and isolate clean geometric contours, and converts the result into DXF format via ezdxf for use in ANSYS HFSS electromagnetic simulation.
mentioned_systems: Chroma; FAISS; BLIP2; LLaVA; LLaVA-1.5; Tesseract; EasyOCR; Stable Diffusion Inpainting; LangChain; LangGraph; PyMuPDF; ezdxf; ANSYS HFSS 2024; DeepErase; YOLO; OmniDocBench
application_domain: Antenna design and electromagnetic simulation; reconstruction of antenna geometries from scientific literature for CAD-based analysis
results_summary: The MRAG pipeline was demonstrated to successfully extract antenna figures from scientific PDFs, retrieve them via multimodal embeddings in a vector database, clean annotations using Stable Diffusion Inpainting, and produce DXF files whose HFSS simulations (return loss, bandwidth, gain) closely matched the values reported in the original papers. The framework was validated on multiple antennas from different studies, confirming generalizability. BLIP2 was shown to outperform LLaVA-1.5 in inference throughput (253.3 vs. 84.9 images/min) and GPU memory usage (2.52 GB vs. 4.09 GB), making it better suited for large-scale multimodal indexing. A reflection-based verification loop using LangChain/LangGraph was shown to reduce hallucination by grounding LLM outputs in retrieved multimodal evidence. Overall, the results confirm the feasibility of an end-to-end AI-driven pipeline from unstructured literature to simulation-ready geometric representations.
limitations: The framework is currently limited to single-layer planar antennas based on geometry; OCR accuracy degrades when image resolution is low, annotations overlap, or fonts are stylized; Minor contour deviations may occur near dense annotation regions after inpainting; BLIP-2 has a significantly longer model load time (701.40 s) compared to LLaVA-1.5 (66.44 s); LLMs and VLMs have a propensity to hallucinate, producing inaccurate or fabricated information when analyzing scientific figures
research_gaps: Reconstruction of multilayer, three-dimensional antenna configurations requires the method to use information from multiple views (side views, cross-section views, or assembly drawings); Multimodal reasoning and structural inference techniques need to be explored to allow reconstruction of more complex antenna structures across a variety of views; Improving OCR detection for challenging annotation scenarios; Fine-tuning the inpainting model for specific antenna layouts

research_focus: Proposing a novel framework that integrates TRIZ (Theory of Inventive Problem Solving) techniques with Large Language Models to enhance the product innovation process, with a specific focus on energy efficiency and sustainability, using publicly available patent data as a knowledge base.
method: The system uses Llama 2 LLM to summarize 3720 USPTO patents with a focus on sustainability and technical contradictions, stores them in a Chroma vector database, and employs RAG technology to mitigate LLM hallucination. TRIZ contradiction matrix is used as a filtering tool, and users interact via natural language queries. The framework is evaluated through two case studies and three experiments.
mentioned_systems: Llama 2; Chroma; RAG; ChatGPT; Bert; Gemini; Mistral; USPTO; Google Patents; Espacenet; Lens.org; Freepatentsonline.com
application_domain: Patent mining and product innovation with a focus on sustainability and energy efficiency
results_summary: The paper addresses the lack of integrated frameworks combining TRIZ and LLMs for innovation by proposing an end-to-end system that summarizes patents with Llama 2, stores them in a Chroma vector database, and uses RAG to ground responses in domain-specific patent data. The system was evaluated through two case studies on sustainable mobile phone device design and three experiments assessing semantic understanding and context awareness. Results indicate the system can provide good support to professionals and individuals for product innovation and problem-solving. The authors also calculated GPU compute time and associated GHG emissions at each stage to address environmental impact. The system produces explainable outputs that enhance transparency and user trust.
limitations: Only patents from a single website (USPTO) are included in the knowledge base; Only patents published in the last decade are considered; The system has not been tested in a cloud environment; No user-friendly front-end interface is provided; Only one LLM (Llama 2) is used without comparison to other models; No qualitative analysis by domain experts has been conducted
research_gaps: Testing the system within a cloud environment; Developing a user-friendly front-end interface; Incorporating and rigorously comparing more Large Language Models with extensive summarized patent samples; Including other patent repository websites (Espacenet, WIPO, etc.) in the knowledge base; Conducting a qualitative analysis by collating domain experts' reviews; Constructing additional use cases to test accuracy and durability of the system; Exploring and assessing quantized LLMs in terms of relevance, accuracy, and consistency

research_focus: Developing a real-time, voice-driven image retrieval system that combines natural speech input with multimodal deep learning (CLIP-based cross-modal alignment) and diffusion-model-guided semantic re-ranking, designed with accessibility for visually-impaired users and hands-free environments.
method: An ASR + NLP pipeline converts natural speech into semantic embeddings; CLIP-based cross-modal alignment maps audio embeddings to image feature vectors; Stable Diffusion is used for semantic re-ranking of retrieved images and generation of query-aligned reference images.
mentioned_systems: CLIP; Stable Diffusion; Google Lens; Pinterest Search; Amazon Alexa; DALL-E
application_domain: Voice-driven image search and retrieval with an accessibility focus for visually-impaired users
results_summary: The paper proposes a unified voice-first image retrieval pipeline that bridges natural speech to visual content via multimodal embeddings and diffusion-guided ranking. It identifies a key gap: no existing system combines full voice input, semantic image retrieval, and diffusion-guided ranking in a single accessible platform. The design targets >85% retrieval accuracy using CLIP for cross-modal alignment and Stable Diffusion for semantic re-ranking. The system is positioned as open-source and designed for hands-free, multilingual, and accessibility-first use cases. The paper remains at the design/proposal stage, outlining architecture and comparative positioning rather than reporting empirical benchmark results.
limitations: CLIP is limited to text-only queries with no native audio pathway; Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPMs) have high computational cost and slow inference; Text-based image search is limiting for users who struggle to articulate complex visual queries in writing; Voice input remains largely unsupported in mainstream image search (over 3.5 billion image searches daily)
research_gaps: No existing system combines full voice input, semantic image retrieval, and diffusion-guided ranking in a single accessible platform

research_focus: Design and implementation of an open-source e-commerce platform that unifies NLP-powered semantic vector search with behaviorally adaptive collaborative filtering for product recommendation and analytics.
method: A three-tier architecture using React.js (frontend), Flask (backend API), MongoDB (persistence and vector index layer), and the Google Gemini API (embedding generation and metadata extraction). Semantic search uses dense vector embeddings with LLM-extracted structured filter predicates; recommendation uses weighted preference accumulation and interaction aggregation for collaborative filtering.
mentioned_systems: MongoDB; Google Gemini API; React.js; Flask; Apache Kafka; Sentence-BERT
application_domain: E-commerce product search and recommendation
results_summary: The platform was evaluated through unit, integration, and functional testing, confirming that semantic search resolved diverse query types (budget-constrained, colour-attribute, occasion-specific, multi-attribute) that keyword-matching baselines failed to surface. The recommendation engine generated personalized product lists reflecting individual behavioral profiles and correctly degraded to popularity-ranked outputs for new accounts (cold-start). Integration testing confirmed the full pipeline returned ranked results within two seconds and recommendation feed generation completed within three seconds. The system achieved superior performance across all eight evaluated capability dimensions while operating at approximately 2-3% of the monthly infrastructure cost of commercial personalization-as-a-service alternatives.
limitations: NLP module does not yet use domain-fine-tuned Sentence-BERT models for richer semantic representation; Recommendation engine does not capture long-range preference patterns (no Neural Collaborative Filtering or LSTM-based sequential modeling); No real-time streaming pipeline for behavioral event processing; NLP query support is limited to English; no support for regional Indian languages (Tamil, Hindi, Telugu); No voice-based search input capability; No explainability annotations presenting recommendation rationale to users
research_gaps: Upgrading the NLP module to domain-fine-tuned Sentence-BERT models for richer semantic representation; Integrating Neural Collaborative Filtering and LSTM-based sequential architectures to capture long-range preference patterns; Implementing an Apache Kafka streaming pipeline for real-time behavioral event processing; Extending NLP query support to regional Indian languages including Tamil, Hindi, and Telugu; Adding voice-based search input via speech-to-text APIs; Surfacing explainability annotations presenting recommendation rationale within the product interface

research_focus: The evolution of database technology from relational systems through NoSQL and Big Data architectures to vector databases, and the role of vector databases as foundational infrastructure for modern AI systems, particularly LLMs and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
method: A conceptual discussion tracing the historical evolution of data management paradigms (RDBMS, NoSQL, Big Data) and positioning vector database technology within the current AI adoption cycle.
application_domain: AI/ML workflows, specifically Large Language Models (LLMs), semantic search, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), handling unstructured data such as text, images, and audio.
results_summary: The paper traces the evolution of database technology from traditional relational systems through NoSQL and Big Data architectures to the current era of vector databases. It argues that vector databases have become the essential backbone for LLMs by enabling semantic similarity searches over high-dimensional embeddings of unstructured data. The paper positions vector database technology as a 'game-changer' in the AI adoption cycle, noting that approximately 80% of organizational data is unstructured and previously difficult to analyze. It concludes that vector database technology has transitioned from a specialized tool to a foundational enterprise requirement, addressing critical challenges regarding data latency and factual accuracy in Generative AI.

research_focus: Automated PDF summarization and intelligent query answering for long, complex documents across multiple domains (research papers, legal contracts, medical reports, financial statements, technical manuals), addressing challenges of scale, layout complexity, context preservation, and domain adaptation.
method: A hybrid AI approach integrating Rhetorical Structure Theory (RST) for discourse-aware summarization, transformer-based models (BERT, GPT-4, Gemini-1.5-Pro) for semantic understanding, and FAISS vector databases for domain-aware retrieval. The system employs adaptive semantic chunking with 127 heading patterns, RST-guided scoring (0.7·TextRank + 0.3·RST nuclearity), per-domain FAISS indices with dynamic cosine threshold tuning, and a hybrid layout processing pipeline (PyMuPDF, LayoutParser+Detectron2, Tesseract).
mentioned_systems: FAISS; BERT; GPT-4; Gemini-1.5-Pro; TextRank; BART-large; T5-3B; FastAPI; Streamlit; Docker; Redis; PyMuPDF; LayoutParser; Detectron2; Tesseract; LayoutLMv3
application_domain: Document AI / NLP: summarization and query answering over heterogeneous PDF documents spanning legal, medical, financial, research, and technical domains
results_summary: The paper presents PDFChatBot, a production-grade hybrid system combining RST-guided summarization, adaptive semantic chunking, and FAISS-powered retrieval for PDF processing. It achieves state-of-the-art ROUGE-L of 0.51 (+16.2% over T5-3B) and F1 of 0.87 (+17.6% over LayoutLMv3) across 50 diverse documents in five domains. Domain-specific F1 gains of 53–78% over generic models are demonstrated (e.g., Legal: 0.49→0.87, Medical: 0.58→0.89). The system processes 100-page documents in 118 seconds versus 8+ hours for standard transformer baselines, reducing document review time by 80%. Production deployment via FastAPI, Streamlit, Docker, and Redis caching achieves 99.9% uptime and sub-second query latency.

research_focus: Few-shot malware detection for newly emerging malware families with limited labeled data, by decoupling representation learning from adaptation through retrieval-augmented inference without parameter updates.
method: Malware binaries are converted to grayscale images, embedded into a semantic vector space using a frozen Qwen2.5-VL encoder, and stored in an external vector database. During inference, query samples retrieve the most similar support embeddings via cosine similarity, and family predictions are generated through similarity-weighted aggregation, enabling adaptation without retraining.
application_domain: Malware detection and cybersecurity (few-shot classification of malware families)
results_summary: The proposed retrieval-augmented framework was evaluated on the MalImg dataset with 25 malware families under 1-shot to 10-shot settings, achieving 0.886 accuracy in the 10-shot configuration. The method consistently outperforms conventional few-shot baselines including Prototypical Networks and MAML. Cross-dataset evaluation confirms generalization across different malware image distributions, indicating robustness against domain shift. Ablation studies demonstrate that combining VLM embeddings with the retrieval mechanism provides consistent improvements over either component alone, validating the effectiveness of decoupling representation learning from adaptation.
limitations: The framework is sensitive to pixel-level perturbations such as Gaussian noise, which significantly degrades performance.; Increasing the number of support samples does not always lead to performance improvement due to intra-class variability.; The computational cost of feature extraction using the VLM introduces latency in full pipeline scenarios.
research_gaps: Improving robustness through noise-aware data augmentation and preprocessing strategies.; Reducing computational overhead through efficient feature extraction and embedding caching mechanisms.; Extending the framework to incorporate multimodal inputs.; Enabling real-time deployment scenarios.

research_focus: Two security issues in RAG agents: (1) the agent not choosing appropriate contextual data from a vector database, and (2) the agent not using the chosen contextual data to generate a response. The paper aims to solve both with efficient zero-knowledge proofs.
method: A KZG polynomial commitment scheme-based zkSNARK is developed to verify that a RAG agent has chosen appropriate contextual data and has used that data in generating responses. The authors prove the proposed verification protocols are secure and scalable.
application_domain: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with large language models, specifically securing the retrieval and usage of contextual data stored in a vector database
results_summary: The paper addresses two security vulnerabilities in RAG agents by proposing verification protocols based on zero-knowledge proofs. A KZG polynomial commitment scheme-based zkSNARK is developed to verify both that appropriate contextual data was selected and that the selected data was actually used in response generation. The authors prove that the proposed verification protocols are secure and scalable. The work provides a concrete cryptographic mechanism to prevent adversarial manipulation or censorship of contextual data by RAG agents.

research_focus: Developing an image-based retrieval method for oracle bone inscription (OBI) character images embedded as static images in academic literature, where conventional text-based search is infeasible due to glyph variability, erosion artifacts, and lack of machine-readable text.
method: A ResNet-50 backbone enhanced with an Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) module extracts multi-scale structural features from OBI rubbing images. The L2-normalized feature vectors are stored in a FAISS vector database for efficient inner-product (cosine) similarity matching. Evaluation is conducted on a self-constructed dataset (OBIs-DIset) of approximately 17,000 annotated OBI images.
mentioned_systems: FAISS; ResNet-50; VGG; DINOv2; CLIP; SIFT; ORB
application_domain: Oracle bone inscription (OBI) image retrieval in paleography and digital cultural heritage
results_summary: The paper addresses the challenge of retrieving OBI glyph images from academic literature by proposing a ResNet-50 + ASPP feature extractor combined with FAISS-based vector indexing. A dedicated dataset (OBIs-DIset) of ~17,000 images was constructed from over two decades of OBI literature to enable realistic evaluation. The proposed method achieves a mean average precision (mAP) of 85.94% and an average retrieval time of 56.25 ms, consistently outperforming handcrafted feature descriptors (SIFT, ORB), classical CNN architectures (VGG), and self-supervised models (DINOv2, CLIP) across all Recall@K settings. The results demonstrate that multi-scale structural modeling via ASPP is particularly effective for the sparse, fragmented, and morphologically variable nature of oracle bone glyphs.
research_gaps: Improving system usability and scholarly utility through enhanced user interfaces and integration of inscription provenance information; Expanding the dataset to include rarer and structurally complex characters to strengthen robustness and generalization; Extending the approach to other ancient writing systems such as bronze inscriptions, cuneiform, and hieroglyphs; Exploring advanced backbone architectures, larger-scale training datasets, and enhanced data augmentation to further improve retrieval accuracy

research_focus: Designing and evaluating SITR, an identity-aware privacy-preserving deep learning framework that prevents unintended sharing of culturally sensitive images (specifically images of women without hijab in Islamic contexts) by combining face detection, identity verification, and hijab classification into a unified pipeline.
method: A three-component pipeline integrating MTCNN for face detection, FaceNet embeddings stored in a vector database for family member authentication, and an optimized DenseNet121 (enhanced with Efficient Channel Attention and hyperparameter tuning) for hijab detection. The model was benchmarked against ResNet50, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNet-B0, then compressed via dynamic quantization and deployed as a RESTful API on Render.
mentioned_systems: MTCNN; FaceNet; DenseNet121; ResNet50; MobileNetV2; EfficientNet-B0; Render
application_domain: Culturally sensitive image privacy protection and content moderation in the Islamic cultural context (hijab detection and identity-conditioned privacy enforcement before image sharing)
results_summary: The SITR framework was developed as a unified pipeline combining face detection (MTCNN), identity verification (FaceNet embeddings in a vector database), and hijab classification (DenseNet121 with ECA). The optimized DenseNet121 achieved 92.16% test accuracy, 91.63% precision, and 86.39% F1-score on a held-out test set of 2,191 images. Dynamic quantization reduced the model size from 82 MB to 27 MB, enabling deployment as a lightweight RESTful API. Qualitative testing confirmed the system correctly allowed sharing of hijabi family members' photos and automatically blurred non-hijabi family members' faces. Average inference time was approximately 19 seconds per image on a CPU-only cloud instance, acceptable for manual sharing workflows but not suitable for real-time streaming.
limitations: Small and geographically constrained training dataset of only 2,191 images with a minimal validation split of 63 images, limiting generalizability to diverse populations and hijab styles; No end-to-end pipeline evaluation was conducted; compounded error across the three-stage pipeline in realistic multi-face scenarios remains unmeasured; Restricted cultural scope: the framework is designed only for the Islamic context and does not account for non-religious head coverings or other cultural/religious traditions; The cosine similarity threshold of 0.7 for face verification was selected empirically without a formal ROC-based analysis; Average inference time of approximately 19 seconds per image on CPU is not suitable for real-time streaming applications
research_gaps: Collecting larger, more culturally and demographically diverse hijab detection datasets and applying cross-dataset validation; Conducting a full end-to-end pipeline evaluation with realistic multi-face test scenarios to measure true system-level precision and error propagation; Performing formal ROC curve analysis for threshold selection in the face verification component; Exploring GPU-optimized and lighter model architectures to reduce inference latency below approximately 19 seconds per image for real-time or near-real-time privacy enforcement

research_focus: The paper addresses the gap in reactive IT operations by proposing IntelliOps, a seven-layer agentic AIOps platform that integrates LLM-based reasoning, RAG-based persistent incident memory, hybrid anomaly detection, and behavioral self-healing for autonomous IT infrastructure monitoring and end-to-end incident resolution.
method: A seven-layer agentic architecture implemented as a PyQt6 desktop application combining: (1) a hybrid tri-modal alert engine (deterministic rules + Isolation Forest + stacked LSTM for 15-minute CPU prediction), (2) a three-stage ASK→LEARN→AUTO behavioral self-healing loop with confidence-based rule promotion, (3) a LangGraph ReAct StateGraph reasoning agent powered by Google Gemini 1.5 Flash with 15 LangChain tools, and (4) a RAG memory subsystem using ChromaDB and all-MiniLM-L6-v2 384-dimension sentence embeddings for top-3 similar incident retrieval.
mentioned_systems: IntelliOps; LangGraph; Google Gemini 1.5 Flash; ChromaDB; all-MiniLM-L6-v2; PyQt6; psutil; Nagios; Zabbix; Datadog; LangChain; Ollama; Llama 3; GPT-4o; Claude 3.5 Sonnet; Mistral Large; SQLite
application_domain: IT infrastructure monitoring, AIOps, and autonomous incident management for enterprise server and desktop systems
results_summary: The paper presents IntelliOps v2.0 and evaluates it across four dimensions using 23,190 real telemetry samples collected over 133 days. The LSTM predictive model achieved a MAE of 6.93% and RMSE of 10.63%, successfully issuing a predictive alert 76 seconds before a critical disk issue during live testing. The Isolation Forest component detected unusual system behavior patterns, and the agentic reasoning layer autonomously diagnosed a Chrome memory leak and cleared 4.1 GB of disk space in a single reasoning cycle. The RAG-based ChromaDB memory system enabled persistent learning, with 12 remediation actions logged across all three self-healing stages. The authors note that no prior AIOps platform demonstrated this level of integrated autonomous behavior, though they acknowledge some components require further testing.
limitations: The system currently monitors only a single machine and does not support multi-node enterprise monitoring; Class imbalance in the LSTM training data (only 6 critical events out of over 23,000 samples) limits the model's ability to detect boundary behaviors under severe conditions; The PyQt6 desktop application requires local installation and does not offer remote or mobile access; The authors express uncertainty about how consistently the LSTM provides advance warning at the demonstrated level; The authors note that some parts of the system might need more testing before full production deployment
research_gaps: Extending IntelliOps to multi-node enterprise monitoring with a central server correlating anomalies across machines, potentially using gRPC for lightweight telemetry; Addressing LSTM class imbalance using SMOTE oversampling or class-weighted losses to improve detection of critical events; Benchmarking alternative LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Mistral Large) on an IntelliOps-specific tool-use evaluation to guide model selection based on latency and deployment constraints; Replacing the fixed-threshold self-healing promotion rule with a reinforcement learning approach that adapts thresholds per process or user based on post-heal CPU improvement; Developing a mobile app or web dashboard with a REST API over the existing SQLite and ChromaDB backend for 24/7 remote alert acknowledgment

research_focus: Addressing the limitations of monolithic LLM pipelines in AI-assisted technical hiring (domain shallowness, evaluation inconsistency, limited interpretability) by proposing a skill-routed multi-agent architecture that dynamically delegates candidate evaluation to domain-specialized expert agents.
method: A multi-agent architecture (SRMAH) with a switch-based orchestration layer that maps extracted candidate skills to domain clusters and routes evaluation to specialized agents (Backend, Frontend, DevOps, Data, Behavioral). The system includes an embedding-augmented semantic routing layer with vector embeddings, semantic skill graphs, and retrieval-augmented candidate-job alignment, followed by synthesis via an Interview Orchestrator Agent and a Decision Arbiter Agent.
application_domain: AI-assisted technical hiring, resume screening, candidate-job matching, and adaptive interview generation
results_summary: The paper proposes SRMAH, a multi-agent architecture that decomposes the hiring workflow into specialized agents (Resume Parsing, Skill Router, Specialist Evaluation, Interview Orchestrator, and Decision Arbiter) to overcome the domain shallowness and inconsistency of monolithic LLM pipelines. A switch-based orchestration layer dynamically routes candidate evaluation to domain-specialized expert agents based on inferred skill topology extracted from resumes. The architecture is designed to improve candidate-role alignment, scoring interpretability, and adaptive interview generation tailored to domain-specific expertise. The paper presents the system design, routing strategy, evaluation methodology, and a comparative framework against single-agent baselines. The proposed architecture is positioned as a reproducible and extensible framework for intelligent technical hiring in enterprise AI decision systems.
limitations: Higher orchestration complexity compared to monolithic baselines; Increased latency compared to monolithic baselines; Additional inference cost compared to monolithic baselines; Routing quality depends on skill extraction fidelity; Evaluator performance remains sensitive to prompt design and domain calibration

research_focus: Proposing and evaluating the AssetHub AI Assistant, an LLM-driven natural language querying framework for industrial asset data structured according to the Asset Administration Shell (AAS) standard, using a Retrieval-Augmented Generation architecture with vector databases for context retrieval over NoSQL data.
method: A multi-pass querying pipeline with a Semantic Query Mediation Layer (SQML) that separates a semantic map (PostgreSQL) from a data map (MongoDB), combining vector databases for context retrieval of unstructured AAS data. The SQML balances generative model flexibility with industrial domain knowledge and NoSQL structural constraints. Validation was conducted via a 120-question benchmark across three difficulty levels with comparative analysis against a baseline solution and a two-stage evaluation (structural validity and semantic correctness).
mentioned_systems: AssetHub AI Assistant; OpenAI models; PICARD; MongoDB; PostgreSQL; Spider benchmark
application_domain: Industrial asset management and Industry 4.0 digital engineering, specifically natural language querying of Asset Administration Shell (AAS)-structured NoSQL data for industrial assets such as pumps and manufacturing equipment.
results_summary: The paper proposed the AssetHub AI Assistant with a SQML architecture to bridge natural language queries and complex nested NoSQL schemas in the AAS domain. A benchmark of 120 questions spanning easy, medium, and hard difficulty levels was used to evaluate the system against a baseline. The proposed approach achieved 90.83% overall semantic correctness in retrieving requested information, consistently outperforming the baseline. The McNemar statistical test confirmed that the observed improvements were statistically significant. The SQML demonstrated robustness in handling highly nested, dynamic, and sparse NoSQL structures without requiring model-specific fine-tuning.
limitations: SQML depends heavily on the quality and homogeneity of underlying metadata (schema and data dictionary); with limited or unstructured legacy data, context retrieval can be slower and less accurate; Generalization across numerous large-scale industrial deployments of different domains has yet to be verified; The pipeline was validated only with private LLMs (e.g., OpenAI models); performance with smaller open-source models in zero-shot settings remains untested; The multi-phase interpretative pipeline introduces extra delay compared to hardcoded database queries, posing a challenge for real-time critical industrial orchestrations; Structural validity of generated queries does not necessarily translate to semantic validity in more open environments, such as with semantically-ambiguous language, double negation, or schema mismatches; Graph RAG solutions face a structural barrier when applied to the recursive and nested document structure of the AAS, as reducing hierarchical AAS data to knowledge graph nodes and edges is challenging and potentially ambiguous
research_gaps: Automated and resilient ontological mapping to enable Graph RAG integration for exploiting the hierarchical structure of AAS data; Expansion of the experimental setup to other industrial sectors and additional NoSQL database configurations to demonstrate architecture scalability; Configuration of smaller (sparse and quantized) open-source, finetuned LLMs suitable for near-realtime on-premise industrial servers to reduce dependence on proprietary technologies; Introduction of context adaptive re-ranking for a more resilient context retrieval scheme; Investigation of adversarial cases where structural validity does not translate to semantic validity (semantically-ambiguous language, double negation, schema mismatches); Testing the framework in heterogeneous multi-vendor industrial environments; Performance evaluation of SQML in zero-shot settings with smaller open-source models for on-premise deployment where data privacy and computational cost are essential

research_focus: Identifying and characterizing the challenges practitioners encounter when developing with agentic frameworks (LangChain, CrewAI, AutoGen), examining the types of questions developers ask, and quantifying which technical areas are most difficult for the community to resolve.
method: Analysis of 2658 Stack Overflow posts related to agentic frameworks using co-occurring tag analysis and Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) for topic extraction, manual coding of a representative sample of 1767 posts to classify question types (How, Why, What), and quantitative assessment of topic difficulty via percentage of unresolved posts and median time to accepted answers.
application_domain: Agentic AI framework development and LLM-based agent orchestration, with vector database operations identified as a key challenge area within that context
results_summary: The paper analyzed 2658 Stack Overflow posts to identify practitioner challenges with agentic frameworks, extracting 14 topics grouped into four categories: Data Management (30%), Integration (29%), Development (28%), and Prerequisites (13%). The majority of posts (71.1%) were procedural 'How' questions, indicating a strong need for practical guidance. LLM execution and runtime issues had the highest proportion of unanswered posts at 86%, while vector database-related problems took the longest to resolve with a median time of 100.3 hours. In contrast, library and output/token issues were resolved more quickly (median 11.2 h). No statistically significant correlation was found between topic difficulty and topic popularity.
research_gaps: Designing higher-level abstractions for agent orchestration; Formal verification techniques to ensure correct interactions between agents; Optimized methods for managing runtime execution and vector database operations; Standardized execution workflows, debugging aids, and tools to simplify orchestration and data management; Tailored educational resources providing practitioners with practical experience using agentic frameworks

research_focus: Addressing limitations of LLM-based automated program repair (limited context awareness, repetitive patch generation, inability to learn from failed attempts) through a novel agent-based architecture with dynamic context management and iterative refinement.
method: An agent-based architecture with three specialized agents (Context Updater, Generator, Overfitting Detector) that collaborate through a shared context pool. The system uses a vector database with an embedding model for semantic code search, a static analysis tool suite for context gathering, intelligent hypothesis tracking to avoid redundant repairs, and component-level mapping to decompose multi-function bugs into independent repair targets.
mentioned_systems: GPT-4o; QwenCoder-32B; CodeLlama-34B; Codex; CodeT5; Defects4J; SWE-Bench Lite; GZoltar; Ochiai; Docker
application_domain: Automated program repair for Java and Python software, evaluated on Defects4J and SWE-Bench Lite benchmarks
results_summary: The paper presents an agent-based APR architecture and evaluates it on Defects4J and SWE-Bench Lite using GPT-4o, QwenCoder-32B, and CodeLlama-34B under both perfect and automated fault localization settings. The approach correctly fixes up to 365 bugs on Defects4J and 87 on SWE-Bench Lite with GPT-4o, with open-source models achieving up to 252 correct fixes. Under automated fault localization (GZoltar with Ochiai ranking), the approach retains 69.7% of perfect-FL performance. The architecture is particularly effective on complex multi-function bugs, fixing up to 53 on Defects4J and 10 on SWE-Bench Lite. Ablation analysis confirms that adaptive context management and overfitting detection contribute meaningfully to repair performance, with weaker models benefiting disproportionately from iterative context enrichment.
limitations: The method-centric design and reliance on coverage-guided decomposition may limit the ability to capture broader structural dependencies and handle tightly coupled program elements; The approach depends on benchmark settings with well-defined test suites, which may not fully reflect real-world development environments
research_gaps: Improving agent coordination strategies; Developing more precise context selection mechanisms; Enhancing support for structural dependencies beyond the method level; Extending the approach to better handle complex interdependent code regions; Reducing the computational overhead of iterative repair

research_focus: Addressing the shortcomings of traditional visual SLAM in texture detail modeling and geometric consistency, and the limitations of existing neural implicit SLAM methods in real-time performance and scene scalability, by proposing a hybrid representation that fuses neural point clouds with multi-resolution voxels for dense RGB-Depth SLAM.
method: NPMV-SLAM combines a multi-resolution hash voxel grid for global structural indexing with feature point clouds for local geometric detail. A position-enhanced encoding mechanism fuses both representations, and an adaptive sampling strategy guided by point cloud density priors uses a vector database similarity search algorithm to concentrate computational resources on object surface regions during volumetric rendering.
indexing_methods: multi-resolution hash voxel grid; vector database similarity search
application_domain: Dense visual SLAM, 3D scene reconstruction, indoor navigation, digital twin generation, and virtual reality
results_summary: The paper proposes NPMV-SLAM, a dense RGB-Depth neural implicit SLAM system that fuses multi-resolution hash voxel grids with feature point clouds to balance reconstruction quality and computational efficiency. Experiments on the Replica and TUM indoor datasets demonstrate notable improvements in tracking accuracy, rendering quality, and mapping accuracy compared to existing approaches. The adaptive sampling strategy, leveraging point cloud density priors and vector database similarity search, significantly reduces computational redundancy in empty regions while maintaining detailed surface reconstruction. Ablation experiments confirm that both the hybrid positional encoding and the adaptive sampling mechanism contribute critically to the overall performance gains.
limitations: Reliance on deep learning imposes substantial computational demands, making real-time pose tracking and dense reconstruction feasible only on high-end hardware; Reconstruction quality degrades significantly under challenging real-world conditions such as motion blur, sensor noise, and lens distortion
research_gaps: Development of lightweight architectures to reduce computational demands of neural implicit SLAM; Hardware-aware algorithms for efficient deployment in unconstrained environments; Improved sensor modeling to handle motion blur, sensor noise, and lens distortion in practical robotic or handheld camera applications; Extending the method beyond laboratory settings to real-world indoor environments such as underground parking garages and intelligent warehouses; Enabling centimeter-accurate dense mapping for robust navigation in indoor GPS-denied settings; Rapid digital twin generation of indoor spaces for immersive VR walkthroughs and metaverse construction

research_focus: Designing a multi-modal (text and voice) Retrieval-Augmented Generation system that combines local vector indexing for data privacy with cloud-scale LLMs to provide grounded, context-aware document intelligence for professional workflows.
method: Hybrid RAG architecture featuring edge-based embedding generation in the user's browser for local vector indexing, cloud-scale Gemini 2.0/2.5 LLMs for reasoning over retrieved document segments, and a low-latency voice interaction layer for natural spoken dialogue.
application_domain: Professional document search and intelligence, with potential applications in education, medicine, law, and finance.
results_summary: The paper presents the Oracle AI system, a multi-modal RAG framework that bridges static document repositories with dynamic user inquiry through both text and voice interfaces. The system uses edge-based embedding generation to create high-dimensional vector representations locally in the user's browser, ensuring sensitive data never leaves the local environment for indexing while enabling fast semantic retrieval. Cloud-scale Gemini 2.0/2.5 models provide nuanced reasoning over complex document structures, grounding every response in retrieved segments with verifiable citations to mitigate hallucinations. The paper positions Oracle as a prototype for 'Ambient Intelligence,' demonstrating that privacy-preserving edge processing can coexist with world-class LLM capabilities. No quantitative benchmarks or comparative evaluations are presented; the contribution is primarily architectural and conceptual.
research_gaps: Refining the underlying models for improved responsiveness and capability; Improving the efficiency of edge-based embedding generation; Achieving a seamless, interface-free interaction where the 'Digital Sage' becomes a transparent extension of user memory and reasoning

research_focus: Designing a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-based hybrid memory architecture for conversational AI that improves long-term context management, conversational continuity, and intelligent response generation.
method: The proposed system combines multiple memory types (semantic, episodic, procedural, and emotional) with RAG, uses vector databases for embedding-based retrieval, integrates knowledge graphs for structured reasoning, and incorporates privacy and governance mechanisms for ethical data handling.
application_domain: Agricultural knowledge sharing and domain-specific conversational applications
results_summary: The paper proposes a RAG-driven hybrid memory architecture that integrates semantic, episodic, procedural, and emotional memory layers with vector databases and knowledge graphs. Experimental observations demonstrate that the amalgamation of RAG with hybrid memory markedly enhances response precision, personalization, and long-term context retention. research_focus: Proposing VecBench, a controllable benchmark for holistic evaluation of filtered vector search in vector databases, addressing the limitations of existing benchmarks that rely on low-dimensional data, simplistic random filter workloads, and lack dynamic evaluation scenarios.

application_domain: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for large language models, with examples from e-commerce product image search and internal document search
results_summary: The paper addresses the inadequacy of existing filtered vector search benchmarks by proposing VecBench, which enables controllable data generation with provable error bounds, fine-grained workload control over selectivity and filter correlation, and a unified six-phase evaluation metric. research_focus: Development and feasibility evaluation of a dual-purpose Japanese-language AI agent system that delivers verified HPV vaccine information to the public via a conversational interface while simultaneously generating infoveillance reports for medical institutions based on user interactions and social media discourse.
method: The system comprises three components: a vector database integrating 139,803 documents (academic papers, government sources, news media, social media posts); a retrieval-augmented generation chatbot using a ReAct agent architecture with iterative multitool orchestration across 5 specialized knowledge sources; and an automated report generation system with modules for news analysis, research synthesis, social media sentiment analysis (stance classification, topic modeling), and user interaction pattern identification. Performance was assessed using both automated LLM-based and manual expert evaluation protocols on a 0-to-5 scale.
application_domain: HPV vaccine public health communication, social media infoveillance, and Japanese-language health information dissemination
results_summary: The system was evaluated through simulated conversations generated by 3 volunteers and report assessments by 3 evaluators over 4 periods. Single-turn chatbot evaluation yielded an overall mean score of 4.80 (SD 0.67), with correctness (4.90) and routing (4.89) scoring highest, and 90-99% of responses receiving scores of 4 or higher. Multiturn evaluation showed improved performance with an overall mean of 4.98, with topic centering and identity achieving perfect scores of 5.00. The report generation system achieved high scores across completeness (4.83), correctness (4.88), and helpfulness (4.12), with reference validity reaching perfect scores of 5.00. Validation against human expert assessments showed reasonable alignment for objective dimensions but greater variability for subjective ones, confirming the system's feasibility as a proof of concept for AI-augmented vaccine communication infrastructure.
limitations: The work is a proof-of-concept evaluation rather than a clinical or public health impact study; The system was not tested with real patients, members of the public, or clinical end users in an operational setting; Evaluation relied on simulated conversations by only 3 volunteers and report assessments by 3 evaluators over 4 periods, insufficient for strong generalizable conclusions; Social media data were exclusively derived from Japanese X users, potentially underrepresenting older adults and those with limited digital access; LLM-based evaluation may introduce biases that differ from human judgment, particularly for nuanced routing decisions; The evaluation dataset (31 conversations and 139 exchanges) may not capture all real-world interaction patterns; Keyword-based data collection introduces potential selection bias; Geographic specificity to the Japanese government constrains transferability to national contexts with different regulatory frameworks and vaccination policies
research_gaps: Prospective deployment with real users is needed to assess actual public health impact; Adaptation of the architecture and evaluation frameworks to other vaccines and health conditions; Extension to multilingual public health contexts beyond Japanese

research_focus: RAG architectures in .NET applications, covering the integration between generative models, vector databases, and the OpenAI API, including embeddings, chunking, semantic retrieval, re-ranking, security, and observability in enterprise pipelines.
method: Discussion of practical implementation patterns and best practices for RAG pipelines in .NET, including orchestration with Worker Services, .NET 10-compatible examples, and evaluation metrics (Recall@K, MRR, groundedness, factual consistency) for retrieval and generation quality.
application_domain: Enterprise NLP and text generation with institutional knowledge in .NET-based corporate applications
results_summary: The paper examines RAG architectures within .NET enterprise applications, covering the full pipeline from document ingestion and chunking through semantic retrieval, re-ranking, and generation. It identifies practical limitations such as context saturation, redundant documents, outdated embeddings, and terminological ambiguities that persist even in well-designed pipelines. The authors argue that the most effective improvements come from refining ingestion, document taxonomy, update policies, and re-ranking criteria rather than swapping the generative model. Orchestration practices using Worker Services and .NET 10 are presented to enhance accuracy, traceability, and resilience. The paper concludes that the competitive advantage lies in the quality of retrieval, orchestration, and governance design rather than in the choice of any single tool.
limitations: Context saturation in retrieval pipelines; Redundant documents in the knowledge base; Outdated embeddings degrading retrieval quality; Terminological ambiguities affecting retrieval accuracy; Measuring only textual fluency is insufficient because eloquent answers can still be wrong

research_focus: Providing operational access to current metadata in complex, ever-changing relational data warehouses by overcoming the limitations of traditional static catalogs, specifically addressing metadata staleness, lack of natural-language semantic search, and absence of built-in ETL diagnostic capabilities.
method: A dual-loop architecture combining ReAct agents and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). The first loop (Ingestion Agent) continuously monitors infrastructure changes (DDL, code, operational metrics) and automatically generates semantic descriptions to update a vector database. The second loop (Assistant Agent) interprets natural-language queries, combining dense semantic retrieval over the vector database with direct execution of diagnostic actions (SQL execution, log reading, query plan analysis) through an extensible tool system.
mentioned_systems: Goods; Ground; Aurum; Microsoft Purview; LinkedIn DataHub; OpenMetadata; Atlan; Alation; Unity Catalog; Data-Copilot; RAGAS; MARE
indexing_methods: locality-sensitive hashing (LSH); word embeddings; dense semantic retrieval over a vector database
application_domain: Metadata management and ETL/ELT process diagnostics in relational data warehouses, including analytical query generation from business terms and operational incident diagnosis for data engineering teams.
results_summary: The paper demonstrates a dual-loop ReAct-and-RAG architecture (implemented as the MARE proof-of-concept) that maintains a self-updating semantic layer for relational data warehouses. Semantic search over the vector database achieved Recall@3 = 1.000 for all six test queries, and agent response time was 15–35 seconds compared to an expert estimate of 15–30 minutes for manual execution. RAGAS evaluation confirmed answer consistency for diagnostic tasks (Faithfulness 0.70) and answer relevance in both scenarios (0.72–0.85). The evaluation also revealed that RAGAS metrics Context Precision and Context Recall are inapplicable to agent systems with unranked tool-call results, and Faithfulness underestimates SQL generation tasks. The evaluation was limited to a demonstration warehouse with nine tables, and systematic industrial-scale verification remains future work.
limitations: Evaluation conducted only on a demonstration warehouse with nine tables, not at industrial scale; Metadata standards support (R4), owner information (R7), and access control (R8) are only partially implemented or not included in the current scope; User feedback functions (R12) are not part of the current version; RAGAS Context Precision and Context Recall metrics are inapplicable to unranked tool-call results in agent systems; RAGAS Faithfulness metric underestimates scores for SQL generation tasks where the answer is logically constructed rather than cited from context; Ensuring the reliability of LLM agents remains an unresolved challenge; only a basic verification mechanism (analyze_query_plan) is implemented; The procedure for scenario selection has not been formalized and has not been validated with external experts
research_gaps: Developing a comprehensive reliability system covering validation of different result types, uncertainty handling, and escalation mechanisms; Exploring dialog mechanisms that enable the agent to actively clarify context with the user for short or ambiguous queries; Adapting the proposed principles to hybrid architectures such as Data Lakehouse, including management of non-relational and semi-structured metadata; Developing evaluation metrics that account for the specifics of multi-step agent reasoning; Systematic verification under industrial conditions with hundreds of tables and real workloads; Formalizing the procedure for scenario selection and validation with external experts

research_focus: The paper addresses the challenge of detecting zero-day attacks in network intrusion detection systems by proposing a cognitive, continuously adaptive framework (CNIDS) that integrates continual representation learning, persistent vector memory, and human-aligned feedback to convert zero-day uncertainty into actionable knowledge.
method: The CNIDS framework integrates Continual Pre-Training (CPT) for evolving traffic alignment, Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) for known-attack precision, and a Human-in-the-Loop Reinforcement Signal (HRS) for structured learning updates, all unified through a vector database serving as long-term episodic memory. Evaluation uses a class-exclusion zero-day protocol on NSL-KDD, UNSW-NB15, and CICIDS2017 with ablation analysis and statistical significance testing.
application_domain: Network security and intrusion detection (zero-day attack detection, anomaly detection, malware detection)
results_summary: The paper proposes CNIDS, a cognitive IDS architecture that unifies CPT, SFT, and HRS through a vector database for long-term episodic memory and similarity-based reasoning. Using a class-exclusion zero-day protocol across NSL-KDD, UNSW-NB15, and CICIDS2017, CNIDS raises zero-day detection from 0% to 18.2% while maintaining precision above 80% and stabilizing false positives. Ablation results demonstrate that removing CPT increases drift sensitivity, removing vector memory prevents knowledge retention, and removing human feedback collapses learning to static inference. The framework is positioned as an adaptive learning system emphasizing learning velocity and post-feedback precision stabilization rather than raw automated zero-day accuracy.
limitations: The research does not claim state-of-the-art zero-day detection accuracy under fully automated inference; Human feedback is simulated with assumed delay and label noise, presenting only an upper-bound scenario for analyst availability; CNIDS is an adaptive framework rather than a standalone zero-day detector, requiring human-in-the-loop interaction for full effectiveness; Blind spots in network visibility (encrypted payloads, misconfigured sensors, architectural gaps) can allow threats to propagate undetected; Resource overload in CPU, memory, or analyst bandwidth can degrade IDS performance at scale without proper tuning
research_gaps: Migrating to distributed vector databases for scalability; Incorporating attention-based deep learning models into the CNIDS architecture; Evaluating CNIDS in large-scale real-world network environments

research_focus: Optimizing high-dimensional vector retrieval performance on NUMA-CXL hybrid memory platforms through a bandwidth-compute coupled memory allocation and management strategy.
method: A two-level optimization framework combining bandwidth-aware data partitioning (assigning contiguous vector segments to each memory node in proportion to its measured effective bandwidth) with NUMA-aware, compute-coupled thread scheduling, augmented by a double-buffered CXL prefetch pipeline. The design is guided by an empirically derived three-tier memory access cost model (local DRAM, remote DRAM, CXL).
application_domain: High-dimensional vector retrieval for AI and data systems, including image retrieval, natural language processing, recommendation systems, and multimodal analytics
results_summary: The paper empirically characterizes the bandwidth and latency heterogeneity across local DRAM, remote DRAM, and CXL memory tiers, establishing a three-tier access-cost model to guide data placement and scheduling. Based on this model, a two-level optimization framework is designed: bandwidth-aware data partitioning assigns contiguous vector segments to each memory node in proportion to its measured effective bandwidth, while NUMA-aware thread scheduling co-locates execution threads with their corresponding data segments. A double-buffered CXL prefetch pipeline further stages upcoming blocks into DRAM to overlap memory movement with computation. Experiments on FAISS-Flat using SIFT1M and GloVe datasets demonstrate up to 12× end-to-end performance improvement under high concurrency, with bandwidth-weighted segmentation and thread affinity contributing 11× and CXL prefetching reducing remote access overhead by approximately 10%.

research_focus: Mitigating the cold start problem in recommender systems by proposing a hybrid framework that combines Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) semantic vector retrieval with item-based collaborative filtering, so that meaningful recommendations can be generated for new users or items without any interaction history.
method: Movie titles and genre metadata are combined into natural language descriptions and encoded into 384-dimensional dense vectors using the Sentence-BERT model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2). These embeddings are stored in a FAISS vector database for sub-linear approximate nearest-neighbor search via L2 Euclidean distance. For warm-start users, item-to-item collaborative filtering is applied using cosine similarity on the user-movie rating matrix. The two recommendation scores are blended via a configurable interpolation parameter α ∈ [0,1]. The system is evaluated on the MovieLens dataset (9,742 movies) with 100 test users using Precision@5, Recall@5, and NDCG@5.
application_domain: Recommender systems for movie/content recommendation
results_summary: The paper addresses the cold start problem by building a hybrid RAG + collaborative filtering system and empirically evaluating it on the MovieLens dataset with 100 test users. The RAG component achieves an NDCG@5 of 0.339 compared to 0.0 for collaborative filtering alone on cold-start queries, demonstrating that semantic vector retrieval can produce meaningful recommendations without any user interaction history. For warm-start users, collaborative filtering achieves a perfect Precision@5 of 1.0, confirming its strength in personalized ranking. The hybrid framework, blended via a configurable interpolation parameter, shows that the two components are complementary: RAG provides semantically coherent recommendations in the absence of user data, while CF delivers high-precision personalized rankings when interaction history exists. The authors conclude that the architecture is scalable and suitable for real-time production deployment.
limitations: RAG component has much lower Precision@5 (0.2) compared to CF (1.0), indicating generated recommendations move away from user-specific taste patterns; Recommendations are only as good as the Sentence-BERT embedding model used; a model trained specifically on movie review text would provide a closer fit with personal tastes; Severe sparsity in the user-item interaction data in the MovieLens dataset leads to 0% recall on collaborative filtering; The semantic retrieval component depends only on title and genre metadata, lacking richer content such as plot synopses, director/actor information, or critical reviews
research_gaps: Finetuning embedding models on a domain-specific dataset (e.g., movie review text or plot summary data); Incorporating richer item content representations beyond title and genre (e.g., plot synopses, director/actor information, critical reviews); Developing adaptive schedules that learn to adjust the interpolation hyper-parameter based on the user's interaction history

research_focus: The problem of fragmented, unstructured academic learning materials in engineering education and the development of an AI-powered platform (SCHOLAR) that uses NLP, LLMs, and RAG to autonomously synthesize heterogeneous student notes into cohesive, syllabus-aligned study guides.
method: Multi-format document ingestion with LayoutLM-inspired spatial awareness and recursive character chunking, Siamese BERT networks for semantic deduplication via cosine similarity matching, Map-Reduce and Multi-Agent frameworks for large-scale text synthesis, and a RAG-based tutoring interface anchored to local vector stores (ObjectBox) with on-device AI (Gemini Nano).
mentioned_systems: SCHOLAR (AlgoQuest); ObjectBox; Gemini Nano; LayoutLM; BERT; Canvas; Blackboard; Moodle; Google Drive; Microsoft OneDrive; CollaClassroom
application_domain: Engineering education and academic learning (undergraduate study guide synthesis and AI tutoring)
results_summary: The paper presents SCHOLAR, a platform that addresses the fragmentation of academic learning materials by leveraging NLP, LLMs, and RAG to synthesize heterogeneous student notes into cohesive, syllabus-aligned study guides. The system employs Siamese BERT networks for semantic deduplication via cosine similarity matching, Map-Reduce paradigms for large-scale text synthesis, and a RAG-based tutoring interface anchored to local vector stores (ObjectBox) with on-device AI (Gemini Nano). Empirical validation using BLEU and ROUGE-L n-gram alignment metrics demonstrates that the AI-driven orchestration pipeline can reliably normalize unstructured data formats and reduce administrative preparation friction. The platform successfully integrates multi-format document ingestion, spatial awareness algorithms, and recursive character chunking to handle diverse input types including handwritten notes. The results indicate that coupling advanced NLP pipelines with robust software engineering patterns can mitigate cognitive overload in undergraduate engineering education.

research_focus: Design and implementation of a medical chatbot that combines a large language model (LLaMA-2) with vector-based semantic retrieval (Pinecone) to deliver context-aware medical information on symptoms, medications, and general health tips.
method: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline: medical reference documents (GALE Encyclopedia of Medicine, 637 pages) are segmented into text chunks, converted to vector embeddings, and stored in the Pinecone vector database for semantic similarity search. The LLaMA-2 model is hosted locally via LlamaCpp, LangChain orchestrates the interaction between retrieval and generation, and the whole system is deployed as a Django web application supporting multi-session chat.
application_domain: Medicine / healthcare information retrieval (symptoms, medications, general health advice)
results_summary: The paper addresses the research focus by building a complete web-based medical chatbot that uses Pinecone vector retrieval to fetch relevant medical text segments and LLaMA-2 to generate contextually appropriate responses. The system was experimentally tested on CPU-based infrastructure, and results indicate that it delivers reliable and contextually suitable medical answers with moderately good response times. The authors conclude that combining Pinecone-based vector retrieval with a large language model provides an effective and privacy-conscious approach to delivering healthcare-related information, since the LLM runs locally without external APIs. The chatbot also supports multi-session conversations through maintained chat history.
limitations: Response times are only moderately good and constrained by CPU-based infrastructure; The system struggles with complicated medical cases; Data quality of the medical reference source is a concern; The system does not support real-time medical information updates
research_gaps: Real-time information updates for the medical knowledge base; Multi-language support for the chatbot; Handling of complicated medical cases; Improving data quality of the underlying medical reference dataset

research_focus: Developing AIDx, a locally deployable AI system for physician clinical decision support that integrates with electronic health record (EHR) workflows, and evaluating its performance on medical question-answering benchmarks.
method: Fine-tuning the Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct large language model on de-identified EHR data (MIMIC-IV), optionally grounding responses with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) from open medical references, and evaluating across nine MultiMedQA subsets under a deterministic single-pass protocol with ablation experiments isolating the contributions of fine-tuning and RAG.
mentioned_systems: AIDx; AIDx-Copilot; FAISS; Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct; ChatGPT; GPT-3.5; GPT-4
application_domain: Medical question answering and clinical decision support in emergency medicine
results_summary: The paper presents AIDx, an integrated AI system for physician clinical decision support, and evaluates its core LLM component (AIDx-Copilot) on the MultiMedQA benchmark suite. AIDx-Copilot achieves a mean accuracy of 83.61% (SD 7.37) across nine subsets, with EHR-based fine-tuning accounting for the majority of the performance gain (+17.8 percentage points over the base model) while RAG provides a modest additional benefit (+0.4 points on average). A qualitative error analysis of 200 incorrectly answered items identifies knowledge gaps (41.0%) and reasoning errors (38.0%) as the dominant failure modes. Under a quantized on-premises configuration, the system achieves a median latency of 0.84 seconds per query and fits within 28.1 GB of VRAM across two commodity GPUs.
limitations: Performance reported on public, text-based benchmarks only; no clinical trials, usability testing, or retrospective chart review were conducted; Results should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical effectiveness or safety; The system is single-modal (text) and does not ingest imaging or waveform data; Error analysis is based on a stratified sample of 200 items with manual coding by a single reviewer; inter-rater reliability was not assessed; The ablation study varies configurations on standard benchmarks and does not include clinical task evaluations; Operational metrics were measured on a specific hardware configuration; actual deployment performance will vary with hardware, concurrent load, and query complexity
research_gaps: Conduct an IRB-approved study measuring task completion time, clinician agreement, error interception, and perceived workload with and without AIDx; Expand the error analysis with multiple reviewers and inter-rater agreement; Evaluate failure modes on clinical (non-benchmark) tasks; Compare against fully replicable open baselines under the same deterministic protocol; Expand the system to multimodal inputs where appropriate

research_focus: Detection of series arc faults in low-voltage distribution systems, specifically addressing the high false alarm rate of existing wavelet-based and threshold-based methods when applied to non-stationary load currents.
method: A two-stage approach: (1) differential sliding window higher-order cumulants (HoCs) are computed from current signals to extract discriminative features across seven typical loads, and (2) a symmetric stacked autoencoder (SAE) with three hidden layers (425 neurons total) is trained via layer-wise pretraining with hyperparameter optimization to classify arc fault versus normal operation.
mentioned_systems: SAE (Stacked Autoencoder); HTFNN; DNN; Bi-LSTM; RLMD; SVM; CNN; RNN; AFCI; RCD; GFCI
application_domain: Electrical power systems – series arc fault detection in low-voltage residential and industrial distribution circuits
results_summary: The paper proposes a HoC-SAE method that combines differential sliding window higher-order cumulant feature extraction with a symmetric stacked autoencoder classifier for series arc fault diagnosis. Experimental results across seven typical loads (resistive, capacitive, switching, inductive) demonstrate a detection accuracy of 96.4% with a false alarm rate of 0% and a miss rate of 7.14%. The method achieves a zero false alarm rate, which the authors highlight as a critical advantage for practical AFCI deployment seldom reported in prior work. The lightweight architecture (425 neurons) is noted as amenable to fixed-point quantization and deployment on a 32-bit microcontroller, though recognition rates for dimmers and fluorescent lamps remain relatively low due to their non-stationary current characteristics.
limitations: Fourth-order cumulant computation in the differential sliding window method requires fourth-power calculations, which are computationally intensive for embedded implementation; Recognition rates for dimmer and fluorescent lamp loads are relatively low due to their non-stationary current characteristics
research_gaps: Further research on simplifying the fourth-order cumulant computation for embedded deployment is required; Integrating federated learning for privacy-preserving distributed diagnosis into arc fault detection is identified as a promising direction; Applying cost-sensitive learning to address class imbalance between normal and fault samples in arc fault detection is suggested as a future direction

research_focus: Development and multireader evaluation of a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system for radiologists, designed to provide grounded, hallucination-free responses to reference, regulatory, and methodological queries arising in routine radiological practice.
method: A radiologist-informed knowledge base of 1049 documents was constructed through expert survey and validation. The RAG pipeline incorporated structured document parsing, two-level parent-child vector database indexing, hybrid dense-sparse retrieval, reranking, and a local LLM. Performance was assessed via functional testing (77 queries), automated LLM-as-a-judge metrics (Contextual Precision, Contextual Recall, Answer Relevancy), and multireader expert evaluation by 16 radiologists on 400 technical queries.
indexing_methods: parent-child chunking/indexing; hybrid dense-sparse retrieval; reranking; embedding generation
application_domain: Radiology – reference, regulatory, and methodological queries in routine radiological practice (protocol requirements, safety compliance, structured reporting templates, institutional documentation)
results_summary: The hierarchical RAG architecture was developed with a curated 1049-document knowledge base and evaluated through three complementary methods. No hallucinations were detected in the 77-query functional testing set during expert review. On the full 400-query technical dataset, automated Contextual Precision, Contextual Recall, and Answer Relevancy were 0.735, 0.881, and 0.890, respectively, while expert-assessed Contextual Precision reached 0.886 and mean response accuracy was 4.53/5. Inter-expert agreement was substantial to excellent for most Likert-scale criteria. The moderate correlation between automated and expert-derived Contextual Precision highlighted that LLM-as-a-judge metrics are useful for pipeline debugging but should not replace multireader expert assessment in medical RAG systems.
limitations: The system operates only with textual sources and does not analyze illustrations or medical images.; Knowledge base updating is currently manual, requiring expert validation, parsing, cleaning, chunking, and reindexing, which may delay incorporation of new documents.; The comparison between the RAG system and the LLM-only baseline was based only on automated metrics and was not assessed by multireader expert evaluation.; Retrieval hyperparameters were selected empirically during iterative debugging, and no full latency-performance ablation was performed.; The technical testing set was source-grounded and did not fully reproduce naturalistic workstation queries; no separate holdout-source or real-world user-log evaluation was conducted.; The system was tested on a single-institution corpus focused on organizational, methodological, and regulatory aspects of radiology, which limits generalizability and requires external validation.
research_gaps: Expansion of the knowledge base and development of mechanisms for automated document updates within the vector database.; Partial automation of knowledge base maintenance steps including monitoring of predefined source repositories, detection of newly released or updated documents, metadata extraction, duplicate identification, and scheduled reindexing.; Linking text fragments with associated illustrations or incorporating multimodal models capable of analyzing medical images as part of the response.; Transition from a closed RAG pipeline to an agent-based system allowing the LLM to decide autonomously when external retrieval is needed.; Integrating structured tools beyond purely semantic retrieval to address cases where semantically similar documents are not actually relevant.; External validation of the system on multi-institutional corpora.

research_focus: Detecting suicidal and depressive tendencies among adolescents in social media text (Micro-blog 'Tree Hole'), particularly addressing the challenge of metaphorical and indirect expressions that obscure explicit suicidal intent.
method: Proposes SentinelGPT, which integrates a GraphRAG architecture (knowledge graph combined with a vector database for retrieval-augmented generation) with LoRA fine-tuning of the LLaMA 3.1 model, deployed privately via the Ollama framework. A risk-aware corpus of over 200,000 annotated messages is constructed with fine-grained four-level labels for suicidal and depressive tendencies, aligned with clinical scales (SSI, BDI, CES-D, DSM-5).
mentioned_systems: SentinelGPT; LLaMA 3.1; Ollama; DeepSeek V3; Qwen 2.5; ELECTRA; Sentence-BERT (SBERT); PHQ-9; SSI; BDI; CES-D
application_domain: Adolescent mental-health risk detection (suicidal ideation and depression) from social media text
results_summary: SentinelGPT was evaluated against baselines including DeepSeek V3, Qwen 2.5, Fine-tuned Qwen 2.5, and ELECTRA on both suicidal-tendency and depressive-tendency detection tasks, achieving higher precision-recall balance and superior F1-scores. Ablation studies confirmed that the synergistic integration of GraphRAG and LoRA fine-tuning enables semantic coherence in multi-turn dialogue and interpretable, traceable detection. The model demonstrated particular strength in distinguishing subtle risk-level distinctions in suicidal-tendency classification and in interpreting metaphorical and fragmented expressions. The private deployment via Ollama ensured localised processing of sensitive adolescent data while maintaining detection efficiency.
limitations: SentinelGPT is designed only as an assistive tool; its outputs must be reviewed by qualified mental health professionals before informing any intervention decisions; Confidence calibration of the model's outputs requires further improvement; Fairness evaluation of the detection system is not yet fully addressed
research_gaps: Expanding knowledge sources on adolescent suicidal ideation by incorporating professional research findings and clinical case data; Investigating more efficient fine-tuning strategies such as QLoRA to enhance adaptability while reducing resource consumption; Integrating multimodal data including speech and visual cues to better capture emotional tone and behavioural signals; Improving confidence calibration of the model; Conducting fairness evaluation to mitigate potential biases

research_focus: Designing a unified 'Whole-cycle' Intelligent Video Analytics (IVA) framework for resource-constrained edge devices that simultaneously addresses real-time inference stability, adaptive storage management, and high-speed vector-based embedding retrieval, closing the gap between edge-native compute constraints and the need for scalable similarity search in surveillance pipelines.
method: The framework integrates three core components: (1) a perception-driven closed-loop control law with hysteresis-based state transitions that uses real-time inference latency to modulate GStreamer pipeline parameters (resolution, bitrate); (2) an event-density-based 'Data Diet' algorithm that selectively preserves high-fidelity video during active intervals and compresses static intervals; (3) a hybrid storage architecture combining PostgreSQL for structured metadata and Milvus for CLIP visual embeddings, linked via a deterministic hash key mechanism with a Hash Mapping Consistency (HMC) metric. The system was validated end-to-end on physical edge hardware (Raspberry Pi with Hailo-8 NPU).
mentioned_systems: Milvus; PostgreSQL; AWStream; Chameleon; Hailo-8; Raspberry Pi; GStreamer; CLIP; Node.js
application_domain: Intelligent video analytics for smart city surveillance, real-time object detection and tracking, Re-Identification (Re-ID), and Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) such as vehicle tracking and automated incident detection
results_summary: The framework was validated on a single-node edge testbed (Raspberry Pi + Hailo-8) under sustained computational load. Under CPU utilization exceeding 90%, the three-tier adaptive control maintained a frame loss rate below 0.3%, representing approximately a 13-fold improvement in operational stability over a static configuration. The Data Diet algorithm achieved a 54.2% reduction in total storage occupancy over a 24-hour monitoring scenario by selectively preserving FHD quality during active intervals and compressing static intervals. The hybrid PostgreSQL–Milvus storage achieved a self-retrieval consistency (HMC) of 0.89, an end-to-end hybrid query latency of 34 ms (well within the 100 ms real-time threshold), and a backend ingestion latency of 1.86 ms, confirming that embedding-based retrieval does not impose back-pressure on the real-time edge streaming loop.
limitations: All experiments were conducted in a controlled single-node laboratory environment with uniform lighting, fixed camera angles, and a limited participant pool of one to five individuals, constraining generalizability to real-world deployments; The event density function relies exclusively on the 'Person' class; scenarios involving vehicles or animals are classified as static intervals, leading to unintended quality degradation for non-human targets; The 11% HMC miss rate (1 − 0.89) reflects residual synchronization bottlenecks under peak-load bursts that the current non-blocking I/O architecture has not fully resolved; The impact of dynamic resolution switching between 1080p and 720p on downstream Multi-Object Tracking continuity (quantifiable via MOTA, MOTP, IDF1) remains unvalidated; The sensitivity parameters (α and β) in the utility function are not absolute constants and require empirical tuning tailored to specific operational environments, lighting conditions, and target object classes
research_gaps: Expanding evaluation to multi-node environments and diverse lighting conditions (corridors, outdoors) to validate horizontal scalability and environmental robustness of the Node.js-based asynchronous architecture; Extending the event density function f(D_event) to a multi-class configuration (vehicles, animals) to support diverse monitoring targets; Quantifying the effect of resolution switching on downstream tracking continuity using established metrics such as MOTA, MOTP, and IDF1; Advancing the rule-based control logic toward reinforcement learning-based intelligent algorithms; Integrating Multi-Object Tracking (MOT) and Re-Identification (Re-ID) capabilities to evolve the system into a comprehensive spatial-temporal monitoring solution; Empirical validation utilizing large-scale public surveillance datasets to confirm generalization capability; Incorporating vehicle detection models to explore applicability to Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS)
